title.zh: 卷六十六 列傳第十六: 房玄齡 杜如晦
title.en: Volume 66 Biographies 16: Fang Xuanling, Du Ruhui
title.raw: 卷六十六 列傳第十六: 房玄齡 杜如晦 Volume 66 Biographies 16: Fang Xuanling, Du Ruhui

meta.sourceNote: Body restored from Wikisource juan 66 to match the ChineseNotes chapter heading. The previous Wikisource import used the file number instead of the traditional juan.

sentences.zh: 房玄齡 玄齡子遺直 遺愛 杜如晦 弟楚客 叔淹

translations.literal: Fang Xuanling; Xuanling's sons Yizhi and Yiai; Du Ruhui; younger brother Chuke; uncle Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Xuanling; his sons Yizhi and Yiai; Du Ruhui, with Ruhui's younger brother Chuke and uncle Yan.

sentences.zh: 房喬，字玄齡，齊州臨淄人。

translations.literal: Fang Qiao, courtesy name Xuanling, was a man of Linzi in Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Fang Qiao, styled Xuanling, came from Linzi in Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 曾祖翼，後魏鎮遠將軍、宋安郡守，襲壯武伯。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yi was a Later Wei General Who Pacifies Distant Lands and governor of Song'an Commandery; he inherited the title Baron of Zhuangwu.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yi, a Later Wei General Who Pacifies Distant Lands and governor of Song'an, inherited the title Baron of Zhuangwu.

sentences.zh: 祖熊，字子繹，褐州主簿。

translations.literal: His grandfather Xiong, courtesy name Ziyi, was registrar of Hezhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xiong, styled Ziyi, served as a prefectural registrar.

sentences.zh: 父彥謙，好學，通涉《五經》，隋涇陽令，《隋書》有傳。

translations.literal: His father Yanqian loved learning, was thoroughly versed in the Five Classics, and was magistrate of Jingyang under the Sui; he has a biography in the Book of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yanqian loved learning and knew the Five Classics thoroughly. He was magistrate of Jingyang in Sui times and has a biography in the Book of Sui.

sentences.zh: 玄齡幼聰敏，博覽經史，工草隸，善屬文。

translations.literal: Xuanling was intelligent from childhood; he read widely in the classics and histories, excelled at cursive and clerical script, and was skilled at composing prose.
translations.idiomatic: As a boy Xuanling was quick and bright. He read widely in the classics and histories, wrote a fine cursive and clerical hand, and had a gift for prose.

sentences.zh: 嘗從其父至京師，時天下甯晏，論者咸以國祚方永，玄齡乃避左右告父曰：「隋帝本無功德，但誑惑黔黎，不爲後嗣長計，混諸嫡庶，使相傾奪，諸後籓枝，競崇淫侈，終當內相誅夷，不足保全家國。

translations.literal: He once accompanied his father to the capital. At that time the realm was at peace, and those who discussed affairs all thought the dynasty's fortunes would last long; Xuanling then dismissed those around him and told his father: "The Sui emperor originally had no merit or virtue; he has only beguiled the common people, made no long-term plans for his heirs, mixed the sons of the principal wife with those of concubines and set them to contend with one another; the later princely branches vie in license and luxury, and in the end they will slaughter one another within—they will not suffice to preserve the house and the state.
translations.idiomatic: He once went with his father to the capital. The empire was then at peace, and everyone said the dynasty would last for ages. Xuanling sent the attendants away and told his father: "The Sui emperor has no true merit. He has only deceived the people, made no lasting provision for his heirs, and set the sons of the empress and of concubines against one another. The later princely houses compete in luxury; they will end by destroying one another and will not keep the family or the state.

sentences.zh: 今雖清平，其亡可翹足而待。」

translations.literal: Though it is now clear and peaceful, its fall can be awaited standing on tiptoe."
translations.idiomatic: Though things are calm now, its fall can be waited for on tiptoe."

sentences.zh: 彥謙驚而異之。

translations.literal: Yanqian was startled and thought him remarkable.
translations.idiomatic: Yanqian was startled and thought him extraordinary.

sentences.zh: 年十八，本州舉進士，授羽騎尉。

translations.literal: At eighteen he was recommended as a presented scholar by his own prefecture and was appointed Commandant of Feathered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen his prefecture recommended him as a presented scholar, and he was made Commandant of Feathered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 吏部侍郎高孝基素稱知人，見之深相嗟挹，謂裴矩曰：「僕閱人多矣，未見如此郎者。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of Personnel Gao Xiaoji, long famed for judging men, saw him and sighed in deep admiration; he said to Pei Ju: "I have looked over many men, and I have never seen a youth like this.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Xiaoji, Vice Minister of Personnel and a man long praised for knowing talent, saw him and sighed in admiration. He said to Pei Ju: "I have reviewed many men, and I have never seen a youth like this one.

sentences.zh: 必成偉器，但恨不睹其聳壑淩霄耳。」

translations.literal: He will surely become a great vessel; I only regret that I will not live to see him rise from the ravine and soar to the clouds."
translations.idiomatic: He is sure to become a man of great capacity. I only regret I will not live to see him rise from the valley and climb the sky."

sentences.zh: 父病綿歷十旬，玄齡盡心藥膳，未嘗解衣交睫。

translations.literal: When his father was ill for a full hundred days, Xuanling devoted himself to medicines and meals and never once loosened his clothes or closed his eyes in sleep.
translations.idiomatic: Through the hundred days of his father's illness Xuanling tended the medicines and meals himself and never loosened his clothes or slept.

sentences.zh: 父終，酌飲不入口者五日。

translations.literal: When his father died, he took no drink into his mouth for five days.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he took no drink for five days.

sentences.zh: 後補隰城尉。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed sheriff of Xicheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed sheriff of Xicheng.

sentences.zh: 會義旗入關，太宗徇地渭北，玄齡杖策謁於軍門，溫彥博又薦焉。

translations.literal: When the righteous banners entered the passes and Taizong was taking the land north of the Wei, Xuanling rode with a staff to present himself at the army gate, and Wen Yanbo also recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: When the uprising entered the passes and Taizong was securing the country north of the Wei, Xuanling rode to the army gate to offer his service, and Wen Yanbo recommended him as well.

sentences.zh: 太宗一見，便如舊識，署渭北道行軍記室參軍。

translations.literal: Taizong, upon seeing him once, felt as if they were old acquaintances and appointed him Military Administrative Aide of the Weibei Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong knew him at a glance as if they were old friends, and made him military secretary of the Weibei Circuit.

sentences.zh: 玄齡既遇知己，罄竭心力，知無不爲。

translations.literal: Once Xuanling had met one who understood him, he spent all his mind and strength and left nothing undone that he knew should be done.
translations.idiomatic: Having found a patron who knew him, Xuanling spent himself without reserve and did whatever he saw needed doing.

sentences.zh: 賊寇毎平，眾人競求珍玩，玄齡獨先收人物，致之幕府。

translations.literal: Whenever a rebel force was pacified, the others competed for rare treasures; Xuanling alone first gathered able men and brought them into the headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: After each rebel city fell, the others scrambled for rare treasures; Xuanling first gathered able men and brought them into the staff.

sentences.zh: 及有謀臣猛將，皆與之潛相申結，各盡其死力。

translations.literal: And when there were counselors and fierce generals, he secretly formed ties with them all, and each of them spent his utmost strength unto death.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he found a shrewd counselor or a fierce general, he bound them to the cause in private, and each of them gave his life in earnest.

sentences.zh: 既而隱太子見太宗勳德尤盛，轉生猜間。

translations.literal: Thereafter the Hidden Crown Prince, seeing that Taizong's merit and virtue were still more flourishing, grew suspicious and estranged.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Hidden Crown Prince, seeing Taizong's merit and virtue grow still greater, turned to suspicion and estrangement.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗至隱太子所，食，中毒而歸，府中震駭，計無所出。

translations.literal: Taizong once went to the Hidden Crown Prince's residence, ate, and returned poisoned; the household was shaken with alarm and could think of no plan.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong once dined at the Hidden Crown Prince's residence, was poisoned, and came home; the household was terrified and could think of nothing.

sentences.zh: 玄齡因謂長孫無忌曰：「今嫌隙已成，禍機將發，天下恟恟，人懷異志。

translations.literal: Xuanling therefore said to Zhangsun Wuji: "The rift is already formed; the spring of disaster is about to be released; the realm is in tumult, and men harbor other aims.
translations.idiomatic: So Xuanling said to Zhangsun Wuji: "The breach is already made, and disaster is about to break. The realm is uneasy, and men are looking to other lords.

sentences.zh: 變端一作，大亂必興，非直禍及府朝，正恐傾危社稷。

translations.literal: Once the first sign of revolt appears, a great disorder must arise; it will not only bring calamity upon this headquarters, but I fear it will topple the altars of the state.
translations.idiomatic: Once the first move is made, great disorder will follow. It will not stop at ruin for this household; I fear it will topple the state itself.

sentences.zh: 此之際會，安可不深思也！

translations.literal: At a juncture such as this, how can one not think deeply!
translations.idiomatic: At a moment like this, how can we fail to think it through!

sentences.zh: 僕有愚計，莫若遵周公之事，外甯區夏，內安宗社，申孝養之禮。

translations.literal: I have a humble plan: it would be best to follow the Duke of Zhou's example, pacify the Xia realm without and settle the ancestral temples within, and carry out the rites of filial support.
translations.idiomatic: I have a humble plan: we should follow the Duke of Zhou—secure the realm abroad, settle the ancestral temples at home, and still observe the rites of a son's duty.

sentences.zh: 古人有云『爲國者不顧小節』，此之謂歟！

translations.literal: The ancients had a saying, 'He who acts for the state does not regard small scruples'—this is what it means!
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said, 'He who acts for the state does not stop at small scruples'—this is that case!

sentences.zh: 孰若家國淪亡，身名俱滅乎？」

translations.literal: How would that compare with the house and the state both falling, and person and name both perishing?"
translations.idiomatic: Would that not be better than watching house and state perish together, and name and person both vanish?"

sentences.zh: 無忌曰：「久懷此謀，未敢披露，公今所説，深會宿心。」

translations.literal: Wuji said: "I have long harbored this plan and dared not disclose it; what you now say deeply matches my long-held mind."
translations.idiomatic: Wuji said: "I have long thought the same and dared not speak. What you say now matches the purpose I have kept."

sentences.zh: 無忌乃入白之。

translations.literal: Wuji then went in and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: Wuji then went in and told Taizong.

sentences.zh: 太宗召玄齡謂曰：「阽危之兆，其跡已見，將若之何？」

translations.literal: Taizong summoned Xuanling and said: "The signs of imminent peril are already visible; what then shall we do?"
translations.idiomatic: Taizong summoned Xuanling and asked: "The marks of danger are already plain. What are we to do?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「國家患難，今古何殊。

translations.literal: He replied: "The state's troubles—what difference is there between now and ancient times?
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "What difference is there between the state's troubles now and in ancient times?

sentences.zh: 自非睿聖欽明，不能安輯。

translations.literal: Unless there is a sage of penetrating brightness, they cannot be settled and brought to order.
translations.idiomatic: Without a sage of clear and reverent insight, they cannot be settled.

sentences.zh: 大王功蓋天地，事鍾壓紐，神贊所在，匪藉人謀。」

translations.literal: Your Highness's merit covers Heaven and Earth; the matter is one of pressing the seal-cord; where the spirits give their aid, it does not rely on human scheming."
translations.idiomatic: Your Highness's merit covers Heaven and Earth. The affair is that of one marked to take the seal. Where the spirits give their aid, it does not depend on human plotting."

sentences.zh: 因與府屬杜如晦同心戮力。

translations.literal: He therefore joined with the household officer Du Ruhui in one mind and combined strength.
translations.idiomatic: He and the staff officer Du Ruhui then worked with one mind and combined their strength.

sentences.zh: 仍隨府遷授秦王府記室，封臨淄侯；

translations.literal: He still followed the household in its transfer and was appointed Secretary of the Prince of Qin's household, and was enfeoffed Marquis of Linzi;
translations.idiomatic: When the household was transferred he was made secretary of the Prince of Qin's establishment and enfeoffed Marquis of Linzi;

sentences.zh: 又以本職兼陝東道大行台考功郎中，加文學館學士。

translations.literal: and still in his original office he concurrently served as Director of Merit Evaluations in the Grand Branch Secretariat of the Shaan-East Circuit, and was added as an Academician of the College of Literature.
translations.idiomatic: he also kept that post while serving as Director of Merit Evaluations in the Grand Branch Secretariat of the Shaan-East Circuit, and was named an academician of the College of Literature.

sentences.zh: 玄齡在秦府十餘年，常典管記，毎軍書表奏，駐馬立成，文約理贍，初無稿草。

translations.literal: Xuanling was in the Qin household more than ten years and always had charge of the records; every military letter, memorial, and report he finished standing by his horse—the prose spare, the reasoning ample, and at first there was never a draft.
translations.idiomatic: For more than ten years in the Prince of Qin's household Xuanling kept the records. Every military letter and memorial he finished standing by his horse: the prose was spare, the reasoning full, and he never needed a draft.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘗謂侍臣曰：「此人深識機宜，足堪委任。

translations.literal: Gaozu once said to his attending ministers: "This man deeply understands what the moment requires and is fully fit to be entrusted.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu once said to the ministers in attendance: "This man sees clearly what the moment requires and can be trusted with responsibility.

sentences.zh: 毎爲我兒陳事，必會人心，千里之外，猶對面語耳。」

translations.literal: Whenever he sets forth affairs for my son, he always meets men's hearts; even a thousand li away it is still as if speaking face to face."
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he lays a matter before my son, he always hits the heart of it. A thousand li away, it is still as if they were speaking face to face."

sentences.zh: 隱太子以玄齡、如晦爲太宗所親禮，甚惡之，譖之於高祖，由是與如晦並被驅斥。

translations.literal: The Hidden Crown Prince, because Xuanling and Ruhui were treated with closeness and courtesy by Taizong, hated them greatly and slandered them to Gaozu; for this they were both driven out together with Ruhui.
translations.idiomatic: The Hidden Crown Prince hated Xuanling and Ruhui for the closeness Taizong showed them, and he slandered them to Gaozu, so both were driven from the household.

sentences.zh: 隱太子將有變也，太宗令長孫無忌召玄齡及如晦，令衣道士服，潛引入閣計事。

translations.literal: When the Hidden Crown Prince was about to make his move, Taizong ordered Zhangsun Wuji to summon Xuanling and Ruhui, had them put on Daoist robes, and brought them in secretly to the inner apartments to plan the affair.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hidden Crown Prince was about to strike, Taizong had Zhangsun Wuji call Xuanling and Ruhui, dress them as Daoist priests, and bring them in secretly to plan.

sentences.zh: 及太宗入春宮，擢拜太子右庶子，賜絹五千匹。

translations.literal: When Taizong entered the Spring Palace, he was promoted and appointed Right Mentor of the Crown Prince, and was granted five thousand bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong entered the Eastern Palace he was made Right Mentor of the Crown Prince and granted five thousand bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年，代蕭瑀爲中書令。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan he replaced Xiao Yu as Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenguan he succeeded Xiao Yu as Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 論功行賞，以玄齡及長孫無忌、杜如晦、尉遲敬德、侯君集五人爲第一，進爵邢國公，賜實封千三百戸。

translations.literal: When merit was assessed and rewards conferred, Xuanling together with Zhangsun Wuji, Du Ruhui, Yuchi Jingde, and Hou Junji—five men—were ranked first; he was advanced in rank as Duke of Xing, and granted a substantial fief of one thousand three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When merit was ranked and rewards given, Xuanling, Zhangsun Wuji, Du Ruhui, Yuchi Jingde, and Hou Junji stood first of all. He was advanced to Duke of Xing, with a substantial fief of one thousand three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 太宗因謂諸功臣曰：「朕敘公等勳效，量定封邑，恐不能盡當，各許自言。」

translations.literal: Taizong therefore said to the meritorious ministers: "I have set forth your honors and achievements and measured out your fiefs; I fear I may not have been entirely fitting, and I permit each of you to speak for himself."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong then said to the meritorious ministers: "I have ranked your services and measured your fiefs. I fear I may not have been wholly just, and I allow each of you to speak."

sentences.zh: 皇從父淮安王神通進曰：「義旗初起，臣率兵先至。

translations.literal: The emperor's uncle, Prince of Huai'an Shentong, stepped forward and said: "When the righteous banners first rose, I led troops and arrived first.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's uncle, Li Shentong, Prince of Huai'an, stepped forward and said: "When the righteous banners first rose, I led troops and arrived first.

sentences.zh: 今房玄齡、杜如晦等刀筆之吏，功居第一，臣竊不服。」

translations.literal: Now clerks of knife and brush such as Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui have their merit placed first; I privately cannot accept it."
translations.idiomatic: Now knife-and-brush clerks like Fang Xuanling and Du Ruhui stand first in merit. I cannot in my heart accept it."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「義旗初起，人皆有心。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "When the righteous banners first rose, everyone had the same intent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "When the uprising began, everyone had a mind to join it.

sentences.zh: 叔父雖率得兵來，未嘗身履行陣。

translations.literal: Though uncle led troops and came, he never himself walked the ranks of battle.
translations.idiomatic: Uncle, though he brought troops, never himself walked the battle line.

sentences.zh: 山東未定，受委專征，建德南侵，全軍陷沒。

translations.literal: When Shandong was not yet settled he was charged with an independent campaign; when Jiande invaded from the south, the entire army was lost.
translations.idiomatic: When Shandong was still unconquered he was given an independent command; when Dou Jiande came south the whole army was lost.

sentences.zh: 及劉黑闥翻動，叔父望風而破。

translations.literal: And when Liu Heita rose in revolt, uncle was broken at the mere sight of the wind.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Heita rebelled, uncle broke at the first rumor of his coming.

sentences.zh: 今計勳行賞，玄齡等有籌謀帷幄、定社稷之功，所以漢之蕭何，雖無汗馬，指蹤推轂，故得功居第一。

translations.literal: Now in reckoning merit and conferring rewards, Xuanling and the others have the merit of planning within the tent and settling the altars of the state; therefore Xiao He of Han, though he had no sweating horse, pointed the track and pushed the chariot wheels, and so was able to have his merit placed first.
translations.idiomatic: In ranking merit now, Xuanling and his fellows planned within the tent and settled the state—as Xiao He of Han, though he never sweated on a horse, pointed the way and pushed the wheels, and so stood first in merit.

sentences.zh: 叔父於國至親，誠無所愛，必不可緣私，濫與功臣同賞耳。」

translations.literal: Uncle is the closest of kin to the state, and truly I would grudge you nothing; but I must not, on account of private feeling, indiscriminately give you the same reward as the meritorious ministers."
translations.idiomatic: Uncle is the closest of the imperial house, and I would grudge you nothing. But I must not, from private fondness, give you the same reward as the men who earned it."

sentences.zh: 初，將軍丘師利等咸自矜其功，或攘袂指天，以手畫地，及見神道理屈，自相謂曰：「陛下以至公行賞，不私其親，吾屬何可妄訴？」

translations.literal: At first, generals such as Qiu Shili all vaunted their own merit, some rolling up their sleeves and pointing at Heaven, drawing on the ground with their hands; but when they saw Shentong's argument fail, they said to one another: "His Majesty distributes rewards with perfect fairness and does not favor his own kin—how can we make reckless complaints?"
translations.idiomatic: At first generals such as Qiu Shili had all boasted of their own merit, some rolling up their sleeves, pointing at Heaven and drawing on the ground. When they saw Shentong lose the argument they said to one another: "His Majesty rewards by public justice and does not favor his own kin. How can we complain?"

sentences.zh: 三年，拜太子少師，固讓不受，攝太子詹事，兼禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed Junior Preceptor of the Crown Prince; he firmly declined and would not accept, and served as acting Director of the Crown Prince's Household, concurrently Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was named Junior Preceptor of the Crown Prince. He firmly declined, and instead served as acting Director of the Crown Prince's Household and concurrent Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 明年，代長孫無忌爲尚書左僕射，改封魏國公，監修國史。

translations.literal: The next year he replaced Zhangsun Wuji as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, was re-enfeoffed Duke of Wei, and supervised the compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he succeeded Zhangsun Wuji as Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, was re-enfeoffed Duke of Wei, and was made supervisor of the national history.

sentences.zh: 既任總百司，虔恭夙夜，盡心竭節，不欲一物失所。

translations.literal: Once he was charged with the general direction of the hundred offices, he was reverent day and night, spent his mind and exhausted his integrity, and did not wish a single thing to lose its proper place.
translations.idiomatic: Once he directed the hundred offices he was reverent night and day, spent himself without reserve, and would not let a single matter fall out of place.

sentences.zh: 聞人有善，若己有之。

translations.literal: When he heard of another's good, it was as if he possessed it himself.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard of another's virtue, he felt it as his own.

sentences.zh: 明達吏事，飾以文學，審定法令，意在寬平。

translations.literal: He understood administrative affairs clearly, adorned them with literary learning, and in examining and fixing statutes his intent was toward leniency and evenness.
translations.idiomatic: He understood administration clearly, dressed it in letters, and in settling the statutes he aimed at leniency and evenness.

sentences.zh: 不以求備取人，不以己長格物，隨能收敘，無隔卑賤。

translations.literal: He did not select men by demanding completeness, nor measure things by his own strengths; he received and ranked them according to ability, without a barrier of lowliness.
translations.idiomatic: He did not demand completeness in the men he chose, nor measure others by his own strengths. He took them according to their gifts and did not shut out the lowly.

sentences.zh: 論者稱爲良相焉。

translations.literal: Those who discussed him called him a worthy chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Men of the time called him a worthy chancellor.

sentences.zh: 或時以事被譴，則累日朝堂，稽顙請罪，悚懼踧踖，若無所容。

translations.literal: Sometimes when he was reprimanded over a matter, he would for successive days in the court hall knock his forehead on the ground to beg pardon, fearful and ill at ease, as if he had no place to put himself.
translations.idiomatic: When he was sometimes reprimanded, he would remain in the court hall for days, knocking his forehead on the ground to confess fault, so frightened and uneasy he seemed to have no place to stand.

sentences.zh: 九年，護高祖山陵制度，以功加開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he oversaw the institutions of Gaozu's mausoleum, and for this merit was granted the prestige title Equal in Ceremony to the Three Dukes, with authority to open a headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he oversaw the plan of Gaozu's mausoleum, and for that service was granted the prestige of Equal in Ceremony to the Three Dukes.

sentences.zh: 十一年，與司空長孫無忌等十四人並代襲刺史，以本官爲宋州刺史，改封梁國公，事竟不行。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he, together with Minister of Works Zhangsun Wuji and fourteen men in all, were to have hereditary prefectships; in his original office he was to be Prefect of Songzhou and was re-enfeoffed Duke of Liang; in the end the matter was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he and Minister of Works Zhangsun Wuji, fourteen men in all, were to receive hereditary prefectships. He was to remain in his court office as Prefect of Songzhou and was re-enfeoffed Duke of Liang, but the plan was never put into effect.

sentences.zh: 十三年，加太子少師，玄齡頻表請解僕射，詔報曰：「夫選賢之義，無私爲本；

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was granted Junior Preceptor of the Crown Prince; Xuanling repeatedly submitted memorials asking to be released from the vice directorship; an edict replied: "The principle of selecting the worthy takes impartiality as its root;
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was added Junior Preceptor of the Crown Prince. Xuanling sent memorial after memorial asking to lay down the vice directorship. The edict answered: "The choosing of the worthy has impartiality for its root;

sentences.zh: 奉上之道，當仁是貴。

translations.literal: the way of serving one's superior holds as precious the duty that falls to one.
translations.idiomatic: the way of serving a sovereign holds as precious the duty that is one's own.

sentences.zh: 列代所以弘風，通賢所以協德。

translations.literal: This is how successive ages have enlarged their manners, and how accomplished worthies have joined their virtue.
translations.idiomatic: This is how successive ages have enlarged their manners, and how accomplished men have joined their virtue.

sentences.zh: 公忠肅恭懿，明允篤誠。

translations.literal: You are loyal, grave, respectful, and fine; clear, just, sincere, and true.
translations.idiomatic: You are loyal, grave, respectful, and fine; clear, just, earnest, and true.

sentences.zh: 草昧霸圖，綢繆帝道。

translations.literal: In the dark beginnings you wove the design of hegemony; you stitched close the kingly way.
translations.idiomatic: In the dark beginnings you wove the design of power, and you stitched close the emperor's way.

sentences.zh: 儀刑黃閣，庶政惟和；

translations.literal: You have been the model of the Yellow Cabinet, and the many affairs have been at peace;
translations.idiomatic: You have been the model of the chancellery, and the many affairs have been in harmony;

sentences.zh: 輔翼春宮，望實斯著。

translations.literal: in assisting and supporting the Spring Palace, both reputation and substance have thereby been made manifest.
translations.idiomatic: in supporting the Eastern Palace, your name and your work have both been plain.

sentences.zh: 而忘彼大體，徇茲小節，雖恭教諭之職，乃辭機衡之務，豈所謂弼予一人，共安四海者也？」

translations.literal: Yet you forget that greater frame and follow this small scruple: though you respectfully accept the office of instruction, you decline the charge of the pivot and the balance—how is that what is meant by assisting Me, the One Man, and together giving peace to the four seas?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet you forget the greater frame and cling to this small scruple. You accept the tutor's charge and decline the pivot of government—is that what is meant by standing by Me, the One Man, and giving peace to the four seas together?"

sentences.zh: 玄齡遂以本官就職。

translations.literal: Xuanling thereupon took up the office in his original rank.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanling therefore remained in office at his original rank.

sentences.zh: 時皇太子將行拜禮，備儀以待之，玄齡深自卑損，不敢修謁，遂歸於家。

translations.literal: At that time the Heir Apparent was about to perform the rite of bowing and had the ceremonies ready to receive him; Xuanling humbled himself deeply, dared not present himself in audience, and so returned to his home.
translations.idiomatic: When the Heir Apparent was about to perform the rite of homage and had the ceremonies ready, Xuanling humbled himself, dared not present himself, and went home.

sentences.zh: 有識者莫不重其崇讓。

translations.literal: Those of insight all esteemed his high regard for yielding.
translations.idiomatic: Men of judgment all honored him for that yielding.

sentences.zh: 玄齡自以居端揆十五年，女爲韓王妃，男遺愛尚高陽公主，實顯貴之極，頻表辭位，優詔不許。

translations.literal: Xuanling, considering that he had occupied the chief ministerial seat for fifteen years, that his daughter was consort of the Prince of Han, and that his son Yiai had married Princess Gaoyang—truly the extreme of honor and rank—repeatedly submitted memorials resigning his post; gracious edicts would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanling, after fifteen years at the head of government, with a daughter married to the Prince of Han and his son Yiai married to Princess Gaoyang—honor at its height—sent memorial after memorial asking to resign. Gracious edicts refused him.

sentences.zh: 十六年，又與士廉等同撰《文思博要》成，錫賚甚優。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he again, together with Shilian and others, completed the compilation of the Broad Essentials of Literary Thought, and the gifts bestowed were very generous.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he and Gao Shilian and the others finished the Broad Essentials of Literary Thought, and the gifts were very generous.

sentences.zh: 進拜司空，仍綜朝政，依舊監修國史。

translations.literal: He was advanced and appointed Minister of Works, still directed court government, and as before supervised the compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to Minister of Works, still directed court government, and continued to supervise the national history.

sentences.zh: 玄齡抗表陳讓，太宗遣使謂之曰：「昔留侯讓位，竇融辭榮，自懼盈滿，知進能退，善鑑止足，前代美之。

translations.literal: Xuanling submitted a memorial of firm refusal; Taizong sent an envoy who said to him: "In the past the Marquis of Liu yielded his place and Dou Rong declined glory; they themselves feared fullness, knew how to advance and how to withdraw, and were good at seeing when to stop—former ages praised them.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanling sent up a memorial of firm refusal. Taizong sent an envoy to say: "In former times Zhang Liang yielded his place and Dou Rong declined glory. They feared fullness, knew when to advance and when to withdraw, and saw when to stop; former ages praised them.

sentences.zh: 公亦欲齊蹤往哲，實可嘉尚。

translations.literal: You too wish to match your steps with those past sages, and that is indeed worthy of commendation.
translations.idiomatic: You too wish to walk in the track of those past sages, and that is worthy of praise.

sentences.zh: 然國家久相任使，一朝忽無良相，如失兩手。

translations.literal: Yet the state has long employed you as chancellor; if one morning it suddenly had no worthy chancellor, it would be as if it had lost both hands.
translations.idiomatic: But the state has long employed you as chancellor. If one morning it had no worthy minister, it would be as if it had lost both hands.

sentences.zh: 公若筋力不衰，無煩此讓。」

translations.literal: If your sinews and strength have not declined, there is no need to trouble with this yielding."
translations.idiomatic: If your strength has not failed, there is no need to press this refusal."

sentences.zh: 玄齡遂止。

translations.literal: Xuanling then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanling then desisted.

sentences.zh: 十八年，與司徒長孫無忌等圖形於淩煙閣，贊曰：「才兼藻翰，思入機神。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he, together with Minister of Education Zhangsun Wuji and others, had his portrait painted on Lingyan Pavilion; the eulogy said: "Talent combining flourish of brush; thought entering the springs of mechanism and spirit.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year his portrait was painted on Lingyan Pavilion with Minister of Education Zhangsun Wuji and the others. The eulogy read: "Talent that joins a flourishing brush; thought that enters the springs of action.

sentences.zh: 當官勵節，奉上忘身。」

translations.literal: In office he exerted integrity; in serving his superior he forgot himself."
translations.idiomatic: In office he held to integrity; in serving his sovereign he forgot himself."

sentences.zh: 高宗居春宮，加玄齡太子太傅，仍知門下省事，監修國史如故。

translations.literal: When Gaozong occupied the Spring Palace, Xuanling was granted Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince, still directed the affairs of the Chancellery, and supervised the national history as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong occupied the Eastern Palace, Xuanling was added Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince, still directed the Chancellery, and supervised the national history as before.

sentences.zh: 尋以撰《高祖、太宗實錄》成，降璽書褒美，賜物一千五百段。

translations.literal: Soon after, when the Veritable Records of Gaozu and Taizong were completed, a sealed letter of praise was sent down, and he was granted one thousand five hundred lengths of goods.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after, when the Veritable Records of Gaozu and Taizong were finished, a sealed letter of praise was issued and he was granted one thousand five hundred lengths of silk and goods.

sentences.zh: 其年，玄齡丁繼母憂去職，特敕賜以昭陵葬地。

translations.literal: That year Xuanling left office to mourn his stepmother; a special edict granted him burial ground at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: That year he left office to mourn his stepmother. A special edict granted him burial ground at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 未幾，起復本官。

translations.literal: Before long he was recalled to his original office from mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was recalled from mourning to his original office.

sentences.zh: 太宗親征遼東，命玄齡京城留守，手詔曰：「公當蕭何之任，朕無西顧之憂矣。」

translations.literal: When Taizong personally campaigned in Liaodong, he ordered Xuanling to remain as guardian of the capital, and wrote in his own hand: "You shall bear Xiao He's charge; I shall have no worry looking west."
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong campaigned in person in Liaodong, he left Xuanling to guard the capital and wrote in his own hand: "You shall bear Xiao He's charge. I shall have no worry looking west."

sentences.zh: 軍戎器械，戰士糧廩，並委令處分發遣。

translations.literal: Military arms and equipment and the soldiers' grain and provisions were all entrusted to him to dispose and send forth.
translations.idiomatic: Arms, equipment, and the soldiers' grain were all left to him to assign and dispatch.

sentences.zh: 玄齡屢上言敵不可輕，尤宜誡慎。

translations.literal: Xuanling repeatedly submitted words that the enemy must not be taken lightly, and that especial caution was warranted.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanling sent up word again and again that the enemy must not be taken lightly and that especial caution was needed.

sentences.zh: 尋與中書侍郎褚遂良受詔重撰《晉書》，於是奏取太子左庶子許敬宗、中書舍人來濟、著作郎陸元仕、劉子翼、前雍州刺史令狐德棻、太子舍人李義府、薛元超、起居郎上官儀等八人，分功撰錄，以臧榮緒《晉書》爲主，參考諸家，甚爲詳洽。

translations.literal: Soon after, together with Vice Director of the Secretariat Chu Suiliang, he received an edict to rewrite the Book of Jin; he then memorialized to take eight men—Xu Jingzong, Left Mentor of the Crown Prince; Lai Ji, Drafter of the Secretariat; Lu Yuanshi and Liu Ziyi, Editorial Directors; Linghu Defen, former Prefect of Yongzhou; Li Yifu and Xue Yuanchao, Secretaries of the Crown Prince; and Shangguan Yi, Court Diarist—to divide the work of compiling the record, taking Zang Rongxu's Book of Jin as the principal text and consulting the various other families, and it was very detailed and complete.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he and Vice Director of the Secretariat Chu Suiliang were ordered to rewrite the Book of Jin. He asked that eight men share the work: Xu Jingzong, Left Mentor of the Crown Prince; Lai Ji, Drafter of the Secretariat; the editorial directors Lu Yuanshi and Liu Ziyi; Linghu Defen, former Prefect of Yongzhou; the crown prince's secretaries Li Yifu and Xue Yuanchao; and the court diarist Shangguan Yi. They took Zang Rongxu's Book of Jin as the base, compared the other traditions, and made a full and careful text.

sentences.zh: 然史官多是文詠之士，好採詭謬碎事，以廣異聞；

translations.literal: Yet the historians were mostly men of literary verse, fond of gathering strange, false, and trivial matters in order to broaden curious hearsay;
translations.idiomatic: But most of the historians were men of verse, fond of gathering strange, dubious scraps to swell the store of oddities;

sentences.zh: 又所評論，競爲綺豔，不求篤實，由是頗爲學者所譏。

translations.literal: and the comments they made competed in ornate beauty and did not seek solid substance; for this they were rather ridiculed by scholars.
translations.idiomatic: and their judgments vied in ornate color rather than solid truth, so scholars rather mocked the work.

sentences.zh: 唯李淳風深明星曆，善於著述，所修《天文》、《律曆》、《五行》三志，最可觀採。

translations.literal: Only Li Chunfeng was deeply versed in the stars and the calendar and skilled at writing; the three treatises he compiled—Heavenly Patterns, Pitch-pipes and the Calendar, and the Five Phases—are the most worth viewing and adopting.
translations.idiomatic: Only Li Chunfeng knew the stars and the calendar thoroughly and wrote well. His three treatises—Heavenly Patterns, Pitch-pipes and the Calendar, and the Five Phases—are the parts most worth reading.

sentences.zh: 太宗自著宣、武二帝及陸機、王羲之四論，於是總題云「御撰」。

translations.literal: Taizong himself wrote the four discourses on Emperors Xuan and Wu and on Lu Ji and Wang Xizhi, and thereupon the work was titled as a whole 'Imperially Compiled.'
translations.idiomatic: Taizong himself wrote the four discourses on Emperors Xuan and Wu and on Lu Ji and Wang Xizhi, and the whole work was then titled 'Imperially Compiled.'

sentences.zh: 至二十年，書成，凡一百三十捲，詔藏於秘府，頒賜加級各有差。

translations.literal: By the twentieth year the book was completed, in all one hundred thirty scrolls; an edict stored it in the secret archives, and grants and advancements of rank were each according to difference.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year the book was finished, one hundred thirty juan in all. An edict stored it in the imperial library, and gifts and promotions were given in differing degrees.

sentences.zh: 玄齡嘗因微譴歸第，黃門侍郎褚遂良上疏曰：「君爲元首，臣號股肱，龍躍雲興，不嘯而集，苟有時來，千年朝暮。

translations.literal: Xuanling once returned to his mansion because of a slight reprimand; Huangmen Vice Director Chu Suiliang submitted a memorial saying: "The ruler is called the head; the ministers are named the limbs. When the dragon leaps and clouds rise, they gather without being summoned; if only the time comes, a thousand years are as morning and evening.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanling once went home after a slight reprimand. Huangmen Vice Director Chu Suiliang submitted a memorial: "The ruler is the head; the ministers are called the limbs. When the dragon leaps, clouds rise and gather unsought. If only the time comes, a thousand years are as morning and evening.

sentences.zh: 陛下昔在布衣，心懷拯溺，手提輕劍，仗義而起。

translations.literal: In former days, when Your Majesty was still in common dress, your heart held the wish to save the drowning; you took up a light sword and rose in the cause of righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: In former days, when Your Majesty was still in common dress, your heart held the wish to save the drowning; you took up a light sword and rose in the cause of righteousness.

sentences.zh: 平諸寇亂，皆自神功，文經之助，頗由輔翼。

translations.literal: The pacification of all bandits and disorders came from Your Majesty's own divine achievement; the assistance in civil ordering owed much to supporting wings.
translations.idiomatic: The pacification of all bandits and disorders came from Your Majesty's own divine achievement; the assistance in civil ordering owed much to supporting wings.

sentences.zh: 爲臣之懃，玄齡爲最。

translations.literal: Among ministers in diligence, Xuanling stands foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Among ministers in diligence, Xuanling stands foremost.

sentences.zh: 昔呂望之扶周武，伊尹之佐成湯，蕭何關中，王導江外，方之於斯，可以爲匹。

translations.literal: In former times Lü Wang supported King Wu of Zhou, Yi Yin assisted King Tang of Cheng, Xiao He held the Guanzhong region, and Wang Dao the lands beyond the Yangzi; compared with this case, he may be matched.
translations.idiomatic: In former times Lü Wang supported King Wu of Zhou, Yi Yin assisted King Tang of Cheng, Xiao He held the Guanzhong region, and Wang Dao the lands beyond the Yangzi; compared with this case, he may be matched.

sentences.zh: 且武德初策名伏事，忠勤恭孝，眾所同歸。

translations.literal: Moreover, from the first registration of his name in service at the beginning of the Wude reign, in loyalty, diligence, respect, and filial piety, all turned to him alike.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, from the first registration of his name in service at the beginning of the Wude reign, in loyalty, diligence, respect, and filial piety, all turned to him alike.

sentences.zh: 而前宮、海陵，憑凶恃亂，幹時事主，人不自安。

translations.literal: Yet the Former Palace and Prince of Hailing relied on violence and leaned on disorder, interfering with the times and serving their lord; men could not feel secure.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Former Palace and Prince of Hailing relied on violence and leaned on disorder, interfering with the times and serving their lord; men could not feel secure.

sentences.zh: 居累卵之危，有倒懸之急，命視一刻，身縻寸景，玄齡之心，終始無變。

translations.literal: He stood in danger piled like eggs, in urgency as of a man hung upside down; life hung on a single moment, the body was bound to every inch of daylight—and Xuanling's heart from first to last did not change.
translations.idiomatic: He stood in danger piled like eggs, in urgency as of a man hung upside down; life hung on a single moment, the body was bound to every inch of daylight—and Xuanling's heart from first to last did not change.

sentences.zh: 及九年之際，機臨事迫，身被斥逐，闕於謨謀，猶服道士之衣，與文德皇后同心影助，其於臣節，自無所負。

translations.literal: When the ninth year arrived and the crisis pressed close upon events, he was himself driven away and expelled, absent from counsel and planning; yet he still wore the robes of a Daoist priest and, with Empress Wende, aided in heart and shadow alike. In the matter of a minister's duty, he owed nothing on his own account.
translations.idiomatic: When the ninth year arrived and the crisis pressed close upon events, he was himself driven away and expelled, absent from counsel and planning; yet he still wore the robes of a Daoist priest and, with Empress Wende, aided in heart and shadow alike. In the matter of a minister's duty, he owed nothing on his own account.

sentences.zh: 及貞觀之始，萬物惟新，甄吏事君，物論推與，而勳庸無比，委質惟舊。

translations.literal: When the Zhenguan reign began and the ten thousand things were all new, in selecting officials and serving the ruler, public opinion pushed him forward; his merit and service had no parallel, and his pledge of loyalty was of long standing.
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhenguan reign began and the ten thousand things were all new, in selecting officials and serving the ruler, public opinion pushed him forward; his merit and service had no parallel, and his pledge of loyalty was of long standing.

sentences.zh: 自非罪狀無赦，搢紳同尤，不可以一犯一愆，輕示遐棄。

translations.literal: Unless the offense admits no pardon and the gentry share the blame alike, one cannot, for a single fault or a single slip, lightly show him cast away to a distance.
translations.idiomatic: Unless the offense admits no pardon and the gentry share the blame alike, one cannot, for a single fault or a single slip, lightly show him cast away to a distance.

sentences.zh: 陛下必矜玄齡齒發，薄其所爲，古者有諷諭大臣遣其致仕，自可在後，式遵前事，退之以禮，不失善聲。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty indeed pities Xuanling for his age and teeth and thinks lightly of what he has done, in antiquity there were cases in which great ministers were admonished and sent to retire; that may come afterward, following the precedent of former times—dismiss him with ceremony and do not lose a good name.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty indeed pities Xuanling for his age and teeth and thinks lightly of what he has done, in antiquity there were cases in which great ministers were admonished and sent to retire; that may come afterward, following the precedent of former times—dismiss him with ceremony and do not lose a good name.

sentences.zh: 今數十年勳舊，以一事而斥逐，在外云云，以爲非是。

translations.literal: Now a meritorious veteran of several decades is expelled for a single matter; outside, there is talk everywhere, and men think it wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Now a meritorious veteran of several decades is expelled for a single matter; outside, there is talk everywhere, and men think it wrong.

sentences.zh: 夫天子重大臣，則人盡其力；

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven values a great minister, then men exhaust their strength;
translations.idiomatic: When the Son of Heaven values a great minister, then men exhaust their strength;

sentences.zh: 輕去就，則物不自安。

translations.literal: when going and staying are treated lightly, then things do not secure themselves.
translations.idiomatic: when going and staying are treated lightly, then things do not secure themselves.

sentences.zh: 臣以庸薄，忝預左右，敢冒天威，以申管見。」

translations.literal: Your servant, mean and thin, presumes on his place at Your Majesty's side and dares to risk the heavenly majesty to set forth this narrow view."
translations.idiomatic: Your servant, mean and thin, presumes on his place at Your Majesty's side and dares to risk the heavenly majesty to set forth this narrow view."

sentences.zh: 二十一年，太宗幸翠微宮，授司農卿李緯爲民部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year Taizong visited Cuwei Palace and appointed Minister of Agriculture Li Wei Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year Taizong visited Cuwei Palace and appointed Minister of Agriculture Li Wei Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 玄齡時在京城留守，會有自京師來者，太宗問曰：「玄齡聞李緯拜尚書如何？」

translations.literal: Xuanling was then left to guard the capital. When someone came from the capital, Taizong asked: "How did Xuanling react when he heard Li Wei was appointed Minister?"
translations.idiomatic: Xuanling was then left to guard the capital. When someone came from the capital, Taizong asked: "How did Xuanling react when he heard Li Wei was appointed Minister?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「玄齡但云李緯好髭鬚，更無他語。」

translations.literal: The reply was: "Xuanling only said Li Wei has fine whiskers and beard, and nothing else."
translations.idiomatic: The reply was: "Xuanling only said Li Wei has fine whiskers and beard, and nothing else."

sentences.zh: 太宗遽改授緯洛州刺史，其爲當時准的如此。

translations.literal: Taizong at once changed Li Wei's appointment to Prefect of Luozhou. He was the standard of the age to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong at once changed Li Wei's appointment to Prefect of Luozhou. He was the standard of the age to this degree.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，駕幸玉華宮，時玄齡舊疾發，詔令臥總留臺。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, when the imperial carriage visited Yuhua Palace, Xuanling's old illness flared; an edict ordered him to lie abed and hold overall charge at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year, when the imperial carriage visited Yuhua Palace, Xuanling's old illness flared; an edict ordered him to lie abed and hold overall charge at the capital.

sentences.zh: 及漸篤，追赴宮所，乘擔輿入殿，將至御座乃下。

translations.literal: When his illness grew severe, he was summoned to the palace; he entered the hall in a litter and did not step down until he reached the imperial seat.
translations.idiomatic: When his illness grew severe, he was summoned to the palace; he entered the hall in a litter and did not step down until he reached the imperial seat.

sentences.zh: 太宗對之流涕，玄齡亦感咽不能自勝。

translations.literal: Taizong wept facing him, and Xuanling also choked with grief and could not master himself.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong wept facing him, and Xuanling also choked with grief and could not master himself.

sentences.zh: 敕遣名醫救療，尚食毎日供禦膳。

translations.literal: An edict sent famous physicians to treat him, and the Imperial Kitchen daily supplied imperial fare.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent famous physicians to treat him, and the Imperial Kitchen daily supplied imperial fare.

sentences.zh: 若微得減損，太宗即喜見顏色；

translations.literal: If he improved even slightly, Taizong at once showed joy in his countenance;
translations.idiomatic: If he improved even slightly, Taizong at once showed joy in his countenance;

sentences.zh: 如聞增劇，便爲改容悽愴。

translations.literal: if word came that he had worsened, Taizong's face changed to sorrow.
translations.idiomatic: if word came that he had worsened, Taizong's face changed to sorrow.

sentences.zh: 玄齡因謂諸子曰：「吾自度危篤，而恩澤轉深，若孤負聖君，則死有餘責。

translations.literal: Xuanling therefore said to his sons: "I judge myself critically ill, yet favor grows ever deeper. If I fail the sage ruler, death will still leave guilt upon me.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanling therefore said to his sons: "I judge myself critically ill, yet favor grows ever deeper. If I fail the sage ruler, death will still leave guilt upon me.

sentences.zh: 當今天下清謐，咸得其宜，唯東討高麗不止，方爲國患。

translations.literal: Now the realm under Heaven is clear and quiet, and all is in its proper place—only the eastern campaign against Goguryeo does not cease, and this is becoming a calamity for the state.
translations.idiomatic: Now the realm under Heaven is clear and quiet, and all is in its proper place—only the eastern campaign against Goguryeo does not cease, and this is becoming a calamity for the state.

sentences.zh: 主上含怒意決，臣下莫敢犯顏；

translations.literal: The ruler harbors anger and his mind is set; the ministers below dare not offend his countenance;
translations.idiomatic: The ruler harbors anger and his mind is set; the ministers below dare not offend his countenance;

sentences.zh: 吾知而不言，則銜恨入地。」

translations.literal: I know this yet do not speak, and I shall carry resentment into the ground.""
translations.idiomatic: I know this yet do not speak, and I shall carry resentment into the ground.""

sentences.zh: 遂抗表諫曰：

translations.literal: He then submitted a memorial of remonstrance:
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a memorial of remonstrance:

sentences.zh: 聞兵惡不戢，武貴止戈。

translations.literal: I have heard that troops hate unchecked use, and that in martial affairs stopping the spear is prized.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that troops hate unchecked use, and that in martial affairs stopping the spear is prized.

sentences.zh: 當今聖化所覃，無遠不屆，洎上古所不臣者，陛下皆能臣之，所不制者，皆能制之。

translations.literal: Now the sage transformation extends everywhere, and nothing remote is left out; even those whom high antiquity did not make subject, Your Majesty has been able to make subject, and those whom he did not control, he has been able to control.
translations.idiomatic: Now the sage transformation extends everywhere, and nothing remote is left out; even those whom high antiquity did not make subject, Your Majesty has been able to make subject, and those whom he did not control, he has been able to control.

sentences.zh: 詳觀今古，爲中國患害者，無如突厥。

translations.literal: Looking closely at past and present, there has been no harm to China like the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: Looking closely at past and present, there has been no harm to China like the Turks.

sentences.zh: 遂能坐運神策，不下殿堂，大小可汗，相次束手，分典禁衞，執戟行間。

translations.literal: Your Majesty was able to deploy divine strategy seated, without leaving the hall; great and small khans in succession bound their hands; he divided them to hold the forbidden guard and stand with halberds in the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty was able to deploy divine strategy seated, without leaving the hall; great and small khans in succession bound their hands; he divided them to hold the forbidden guard and stand with halberds in the ranks.

sentences.zh: 其後延陀鴟張，尋就夷滅；

translations.literal: Afterward the Tiele stretched like owls; soon they were destroyed and extinguished;
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the Tiele stretched like owls; soon they were destroyed and extinguished;

sentences.zh: 鐵勒慕義，請置州縣，沙漠以北，萬里無塵。

translations.literal: the Tiele admired righteousness and asked to have prefectures and counties set up; north of the desert, for ten thousand li there was no dust.
translations.idiomatic: the Tiele admired righteousness and asked to have prefectures and counties set up; north of the desert, for ten thousand li there was no dust.

sentences.zh: 至如高昌叛渙於流沙，吐渾首鼠於積石，偏師薄伐，俱從平蕩。

translations.literal: As for Gaochang, it rebelled and scattered in the drifting sands; Tuyuhun wavered like a rat at Jishi; with detached columns and light strikes, all were leveled together.
translations.idiomatic: As for Gaochang, it rebelled and scattered in the drifting sands; Tuyuhun wavered like a rat at Jishi; with detached columns and light strikes, all were leveled together.

sentences.zh: 高麗歷代逋誅，莫能討擊。

translations.literal: Goguryeo through successive dynasties escaped punishment, and none could strike it down.
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo through successive dynasties escaped punishment, and none could strike it down.

sentences.zh: 陛下責其逆亂，弒主虐人，親總六軍，問罪遼、碣。

translations.literal: Your Majesty blamed its rebellion and disorder, regicide and cruelty; he personally led the Six Armies and called Goguryeo to account at Liao and Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty blamed its rebellion and disorder, regicide and cruelty; he personally led the Six Armies and called Goguryeo to account at Liao and Jie.

sentences.zh: 未經旬月，即拔遼東，前後虜獲，數十萬計，分配諸州，無處不滿。

translations.literal: Within less than ten months he took Liaodong; captives taken before and after numbered in the hundreds of thousands, distributed among the prefectures until none lacked its fill.
translations.idiomatic: Within less than ten months he took Liaodong; captives taken before and after numbered in the hundreds of thousands, distributed among the prefectures until none lacked its fill.

sentences.zh: 雪往代之宿恥，掩崤陵之枯骨，比功較德，萬倍前王。

translations.literal: He wiped away the old shame of former generations and covered the dry bones at Mount Yao; comparing merit and virtue, he is ten thousand times the kings before.
translations.idiomatic: He wiped away the old shame of former generations and covered the dry bones at Mount Yao; comparing merit and virtue, he is ten thousand times the kings before.

sentences.zh: 此聖心之所自知，微臣安敢備説。

translations.literal: This the sage heart knows for itself; your lowly servant dares not set it forth in full.
translations.idiomatic: This the sage heart knows for itself; your lowly servant dares not set it forth in full.

sentences.zh: 且陛下仁風被於率土，孝德彰於配天。

translations.literal: Moreover, Your Majesty's humane wind covers all within the four seas, and filial virtue shines beside Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Your Majesty's humane wind covers all within the four seas, and filial virtue shines beside Heaven.

sentences.zh: 睹夷狄之將亡，則指期數歳；

translations.literal: When he saw the barbarians about to perish, he fixed the term at several years;
translations.idiomatic: When he saw the barbarians about to perish, he fixed the term at several years;

sentences.zh: 授將帥之節度，則決機萬里。

translations.literal: when he gave generals their commands, he decided affairs ten thousand li away.
translations.idiomatic: when he gave generals their commands, he decided affairs ten thousand li away.

sentences.zh: 屈指而候驛，視景而望書，符應若神，算無遺策。

translations.literal: He counted on his fingers awaiting the post, watched the sun awaiting dispatches; responses matched like the divine, and plans left nothing out.
translations.idiomatic: He counted on his fingers awaiting the post, watched the sun awaiting dispatches; responses matched like the divine, and plans left nothing out.

sentences.zh: 擢將於行伍之中，取士於凡庸之末。

translations.literal: He raised generals from the ranks and chose scholars from the ends of the common.
translations.idiomatic: He raised generals from the ranks and chose scholars from the ends of the common.

sentences.zh: 遠夷單使，一見不忘；

translations.literal: A distant barbarian envoy, seen once, was not forgotten;
translations.idiomatic: A distant barbarian envoy, seen once, was not forgotten;

sentences.zh: 小臣之名，未嘗再問。

translations.literal: a petty official's name was never asked twice.
translations.idiomatic: a petty official's name was never asked twice.

sentences.zh: 箭穿七劄，弓貫六鈞。

translations.literal: An arrow pierced seven layers; a bow drew six jun.
translations.idiomatic: An arrow pierced seven layers; a bow drew six jun.

sentences.zh: 加以留情墳典，屬意篇什，筆邁鍾、張，辭窮班、馬。

translations.literal: Added to this, he keeps his heart on the classics in tombs and sets his mind on essays; his brush surpasses Zhong and Zhang, his phrasing exhausts Ban and Ma.
translations.idiomatic: Added to this, he keeps his heart on the classics in tombs and sets his mind on essays; his brush surpasses Zhong and Zhang, his phrasing exhausts Ban and Ma.

sentences.zh: 文鋒既振，則管磬自諧；

translations.literal: When the literary edge is stirred, then pipes and chimes harmonize of themselves;
translations.idiomatic: When the literary edge is stirred, then pipes and chimes harmonize of themselves;

sentences.zh: 輕翰暫飛，則花蘤競發。

translations.literal: when the light brush flies for a moment, then flowers bloom in rivalry.
translations.idiomatic: when the light brush flies for a moment, then flowers bloom in rivalry.

sentences.zh: 撫萬姓以慈，遇群臣以禮。

translations.literal: He treats the myriad people with kindness and meets ministers with ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: He treats the myriad people with kindness and meets ministers with ceremony.

sentences.zh: 褒秋毫之善，解吞舟之網。

translations.literal: He praises goodness as fine as an autumn hair and loosens the net that would swallow a boat.
translations.idiomatic: He praises goodness as fine as an autumn hair and loosens the net that would swallow a boat.

sentences.zh: 逆耳之諫必聽，膚受之訴斯絶。

translations.literal: Remonstrance that grates on the ear he must hear; pleas that touch the skin he cuts off.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance that grates on the ear he must hear; pleas that touch the skin he cuts off.

sentences.zh: 好生之德，焚障塞於江湖；

translations.literal: The virtue of cherishing life burns barrier dams on rivers and lakes;
translations.idiomatic: The virtue of cherishing life burns barrier dams on rivers and lakes;

sentences.zh: 惡殺之仁，息鼓刀於屠肆。

translations.literal: the humanity that hates killing stills the cleaver at the butcher's stall.
translations.idiomatic: the humanity that hates killing stills the cleaver at the butcher's stall.

sentences.zh: 鳧鶴荷稻粱之惠，犬馬蒙帷蓋之恩。

translations.literal: Ducks and cranes receive the bounty of grain and millet; dogs and horses are covered by the grace of carriage curtains.
translations.idiomatic: Ducks and cranes receive the bounty of grain and millet; dogs and horses are covered by the grace of carriage curtains.

sentences.zh: 降乘吮思摩之瘡，登堂臨魏徵之柩。

translations.literal: He descended from his carriage to suck the wound of Simo and went up the hall to stand before Wei Zheng's bier.
translations.idiomatic: He descended from his carriage to suck the wound of Simo and went up the hall to stand before Wei Zheng's bier.

sentences.zh: 哭戰亡之卒，則哀動六軍；

translations.literal: When he wept for soldiers dead in battle, sorrow moved the Six Armies;
translations.idiomatic: When he wept for soldiers dead in battle, sorrow moved the Six Armies;

sentences.zh: 負填道之薪，則精感天地。

translations.literal: when he carried firewood to fill the road, his spirit moved Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: when he carried firewood to fill the road, his spirit moved Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 重黔黎之大命，特盡心於庶獄。

translations.literal: He weighs the great mandate of the black-headed people and especially exhausts his heart in ordinary lawsuits.
translations.idiomatic: He weighs the great mandate of the black-headed people and especially exhausts his heart in ordinary lawsuits.

sentences.zh: 臣心識昏憒，豈足論聖功之深遠，談天德之高大哉！

translations.literal: Your servant's mind is dim and confused—how could it suffice to discuss the depth and distance of the sage achievement or speak of the height and greatness of Heaven's virtue!
translations.idiomatic: Your servant's mind is dim and confused—how could it suffice to discuss the depth and distance of the sage achievement or speak of the height and greatness of Heaven's virtue!

sentences.zh: 陛下兼眾美而有之，靡不備具，微臣深爲陛下惜之重之，愛之寶之。

translations.literal: Your Majesty combines every excellence and possesses them; nothing is lacking. Your lowly servant deeply regrets this for Your Majesty, values it, loves it, and treasures it.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty combines every excellence and possesses them; nothing is lacking. Your lowly servant deeply regrets this for Your Majesty, values it, loves it, and treasures it.

sentences.zh: 《周易》曰：「知進而不知退，知存而不知亡，知得而不知喪。」

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says: "To know advance and not know retreat, to know preservation and not know extinction, to know gain and not know loss."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says: "To know advance and not know retreat, to know preservation and not know extinction, to know gain and not know loss."

sentences.zh: 又曰：「知進退存亡，不失其正者，惟聖人乎！」

translations.literal: It also says: "To know advance, retreat, preservation, and extinction without losing the correct mean—only a sage!"
translations.idiomatic: It also says: "To know advance, retreat, preservation, and extinction without losing the correct mean—only a sage!"

sentences.zh: 由此言之，進有退之義，存有亡之機，得有喪之理，老臣所以爲陛下惜之者，蓋此謂也。

translations.literal: From this it follows that advance has the meaning of retreat, preservation has the occasion of extinction, and gain has the principle of loss. The reason this old minister regrets for Your Majesty is precisely this.
translations.idiomatic: From this it follows that advance has the meaning of retreat, preservation has the occasion of extinction, and gain has the principle of loss. The reason this old minister regrets for Your Majesty is precisely this.

sentences.zh: 老子曰：「知足不辱，知止不殆。」

translations.literal: Laozi says: "To know sufficiency is not to be disgraced; to know when to stop is not to be endangered."
translations.idiomatic: Laozi says: "To know sufficiency is not to be disgraced; to know when to stop is not to be endangered."

sentences.zh: 謂陛下威名功德，亦可足矣；

translations.literal: Your Majesty's martial name and meritorious virtue may already be sufficient;
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's martial name and meritorious virtue may already be sufficient;

sentences.zh: 拓地開疆，亦可止矣。

translations.literal: extending territory and opening borders may also be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: extending territory and opening borders may also be stopped.

sentences.zh: 彼高麗者，邊夷賤類，不足待以仁義，不可責以常禮。

translations.literal: That Goguryeo is a base barbarian of the borderlands, unworthy of being treated with benevolence and righteousness, and not to be charged with ordinary ritual.
translations.idiomatic: That Goguryeo is a base barbarian of the borderlands, unworthy of being treated with benevolence and righteousness, and not to be charged with ordinary ritual.

sentences.zh: 古來以魚鱉畜之，宜從闊略。

translations.literal: From antiquity it has been kept like fish and turtles; one should follow a broad indulgence.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity it has been kept like fish and turtles; one should follow a broad indulgence.

sentences.zh: 若必欲絶其種類，恐獸窮則搏。

translations.literal: If one must utterly cut off its kind, I fear that when beasts are cornered they will fight.
translations.idiomatic: If one must utterly cut off its kind, I fear that when beasts are cornered they will fight.

sentences.zh: 且陛下毎決一死囚，必令三覆五奏，進素食、停音樂者，蓋以人命所重，感動聖慈也。

translations.literal: Moreover, whenever Your Majesty decides a death sentence, he always orders three reviews and five submissions, vegetarian food, and the stopping of music—because human life is weighty and moves the sage compassion.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, whenever Your Majesty decides a death sentence, he always orders three reviews and five submissions, vegetarian food, and the stopping of music—because human life is weighty and moves the sage compassion.

sentences.zh: 況今兵士之徒，無一罪戾，無故驅之於行陣之間，委之於鋒刃之下，使肝腦塗地，魂魄無歸，令其老父孤兒、寡妻慈母，望轊車而掩泣，抱枯骨以摧心，足以變動陰陽，感傷和氣，實天下冤痛也。

translations.literal: How much more now are the soldiers, not one of whom has guilt, driven without cause into the ranks of battle and cast under the edge of blades, so that livers and brains smear the ground and souls have nowhere to return—making old fathers, orphaned sons, widowed wives, and loving mothers gaze at the supply carts and cover their faces weeping, embrace dry bones and break their hearts—enough to shift yin and yang and wound harmonious qi; this is truly the wrong and pain of the realm under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: How much more now are the soldiers, not one of whom has guilt, driven without cause into the ranks of battle and cast under the edge of blades, so that livers and brains smear the ground and souls have nowhere to return—making old fathers, orphaned sons, widowed wives, and loving mothers gaze at the supply carts and cover their faces weeping, embrace dry bones and break their hearts—enough to shift yin and yang and wound harmonious qi; this is truly the wrong and pain of the realm under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 且兵者兇器，戰者危事，不得已而用之。

translations.literal: Moreover, troops are an inauspicious instrument and battle a perilous affair; they are used only when there is no choice.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, troops are an inauspicious instrument and battle a perilous affair; they are used only when there is no choice.

sentences.zh: 向使高麗違失臣節，陛下誅之可也；

translations.literal: If Goguryeo had failed in the duty of a subject, Your Majesty might punish it;
translations.idiomatic: If Goguryeo had failed in the duty of a subject, Your Majesty might punish it;

sentences.zh: 侵擾百姓，而陛下滅之可也；

translations.literal: if it had harassed the people, Your Majesty might destroy it;
translations.idiomatic: if it had harassed the people, Your Majesty might destroy it;

sentences.zh: 久長能爲中國患，而陛下除之可也。

translations.literal: if for long it could become a calamity to China, Your Majesty might remove it.
translations.idiomatic: if for long it could become a calamity to China, Your Majesty might remove it.

sentences.zh: 有一於此，雖日殺萬夫，不足爲愧。

translations.literal: If any one of these three were present, though ten thousand men were killed in a day, it would not be shame.
translations.idiomatic: If any one of these three were present, though ten thousand men were killed in a day, it would not be shame.

sentences.zh: 今無此三條，坐煩中國，內爲舊王雪恥，外爲新羅報仇，豈非所存者小，所損者大？

translations.literal: Now none of these three is present, yet China is troubled for nothing—within, to wipe away the old king's shame; without, to avenge Silla. Is not what is kept small and what is lost great?
translations.idiomatic: Now none of these three is present, yet China is troubled for nothing—within, to wipe away the old king's shame; without, to avenge Silla. Is not what is kept small and what is lost great?

sentences.zh: 願陛下遵皇祖老子止足之誡，以保萬代巍巍之名。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty would follow the imperial ancestor Laozi's admonition of stopping when sufficient, to preserve the lofty name for ten thousand generations.
translations.idiomatic: I wish Your Majesty would follow the imperial ancestor Laozi's admonition of stopping when sufficient, to preserve the lofty name for ten thousand generations.

sentences.zh: 發霈然之恩，降寬大之詔，順陽春以布澤，許高麗以自新。

translations.literal: Send forth overflowing favor, issue a broad and lenient edict, follow the spring sun in spreading bounty, and allow Goguryeo to renew itself.
translations.idiomatic: Send forth overflowing favor, issue a broad and lenient edict, follow the spring sun in spreading bounty, and allow Goguryeo to renew itself.

sentences.zh: 焚淩波之船，罷應募之眾，自然華夷慶賴，遠肅邇安。

translations.literal: Burn the wave-crossing ships, dismiss the recruited masses—then naturally Chinese and barbarians will rejoice in dependence, the distant will be reverent and the near secure.
translations.idiomatic: Burn the wave-crossing ships, dismiss the recruited masses—then naturally Chinese and barbarians will rejoice in dependence, the distant will be reverent and the near secure.

sentences.zh: 臣老病三公，旦夕入地，所恨竟無塵露，微增海嶽。

translations.literal: Your servant, old and ill among the Three Dukes, will enter the ground morning and evening; what he regrets is that he can add not even dust or dew to sea and mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant, old and ill among the Three Dukes, will enter the ground morning and evening; what he regrets is that he can add not even dust or dew to sea and mountain.

sentences.zh: 謹罄殘魂餘息，預代結草之誠。

translations.literal: I respectfully exhaust the remnant soul and lingering breath to offer beforehand the sincerity of tying grass.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully exhaust the remnant soul and lingering breath to offer beforehand the sincerity of tying grass.

sentences.zh: 倘蒙錄此哀鳴，即臣死且不朽。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty records this mournful cry, then your servant, though dead, will not decay.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty records this mournful cry, then your servant, though dead, will not decay.

sentences.zh: 太宗見表，謂玄齡子婦高陽公主曰：「此人危惙如此，尚能憂我國家。」

translations.literal: When Taizong saw the memorial, he said to Xuanling's daughter-in-law, Princess Gaoyang: "This man is so critically ill, yet he can still worry for our state."
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong saw the memorial, he said to Xuanling's daughter-in-law, Princess Gaoyang: "This man is so critically ill, yet he can still worry for our state."

sentences.zh: 後疾增劇，遂鑿苑牆開門，累遣中使候問。

translations.literal: Afterward his illness grew worse; they broke through the garden wall and opened a gate, and repeatedly sent palace envoys to inquire.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward his illness grew worse; they broke through the garden wall and opened a gate, and repeatedly sent palace envoys to inquire.

sentences.zh: 上又親臨，握手敘別，悲不自勝。

translations.literal: The emperor also came in person, clasped his hand in farewell, and could not master his grief.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also came in person, clasped his hand in farewell, and could not master his grief.

sentences.zh: 皇太子亦就之與之訣。

translations.literal: The Crown Prince also went to him and took leave.
translations.idiomatic: The Crown Prince also went to him and took leave.

sentences.zh: 即日授其子遺愛右衞中郎將，遺則中散大夫，使及目前，見其通顯。

translations.literal: That same day he appointed his son Yiai Right Captain of the Palace Guard and Yize Palace Attendant, so that before his eyes they saw their advancement.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he appointed his son Yiai Right Captain of the Palace Guard and Yize Palace Attendant, so that before his eyes they saw their advancement.

sentences.zh: 尋薨，年七十。

translations.literal: Soon after he died, aged seventy.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he died, aged seventy.

sentences.zh: 廢朝三日，冊贈太尉、并州都督，諡曰文昭，給東園秘器，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: Court mourning was suspended for three days. He was enfeoffed posthumously as Grand Commandant and Area Commander of Bingzhou, with the posthumous title Wenzhao; the Eastern Garden secret vessels were granted, and he was buried with honor at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: Court mourning was suspended for three days. He was enfeoffed posthumously as Grand Commandant and Area Commander of Bingzhou, with the posthumous title Wenzhao; the Eastern Garden secret vessels were granted, and he was buried with honor at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 玄齡嘗誡諸子以驕奢沉溺，必不可以地望淩人，故集古今聖賢家誡，書於屏風，令各取一具，謂曰：「若能留意，足以保身成名。」

translations.literal: Xuanling once admonished his sons against pride, luxury, and dissipation, saying they must never rely on family standing to look down on others; he therefore gathered admonitions of sage and worthy families from past and present, wrote them on screen panels, had each take one, and said: "If you can heed this, it will suffice to preserve the person and make a name."
translations.idiomatic: Xuanling once admonished his sons against pride, luxury, and dissipation, saying they must never rely on family standing to look down on others; he therefore gathered admonitions of sage and worthy families from past and present, wrote them on screen panels, had each take one, and said: "If you can heed this, it will suffice to preserve yourself and make a name."

sentences.zh: 又云：「袁家累葉忠節，是吾所尚，汝宜師之。」

translations.literal: He also said: "The Yuan family through successive generations has shown loyal integrity; this is what I esteem—you should take them as teachers."
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "The Yuan family through successive generations has shown loyal integrity; this is what I esteem—you should take them as teachers."

sentences.zh: 高宗嗣位，詔配享太宗廟庭。

translations.literal: When Gaozong succeeded the throne, an edict ordered Xuanling to share sacrifice in Taizong's temple court.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong succeeded the throne, an edict ordered Xuanling to share sacrifice in Taizong's temple court.

sentences.zh: 子遺直嗣，永徽初爲禮部尚書、汴州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Yizhi inherited the title; at the beginning of Yonghui he was Minister of Rites and Prefect of Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yizhi inherited the title; at the beginning of Yonghui he was Minister of Rites and Prefect of Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 次子遺愛，尚太宗女高陽公主，拜駙馬都尉，官至太府卿、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: The second son Yiai married Taizong's daughter Princess Gaoyang, was appointed Commandant Escort of the Emperor's Son-in-law, and reached Grand Minister of the Court of the Imperial Granary and Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The second son Yiai married Taizong's daughter Princess Gaoyang, was appointed Commandant Escort of the Emperor's Son-in-law, and reached Grand Minister of the Court of the Imperial Granary and Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 初，主有寵於太宗，故遺愛特承恩遇，與諸主婿禮秩絶異。

translations.literal: At first the princess had Taizong's favor, and so Yiai especially received gracious treatment; his ritual rank and salary differed utterly from the other imperial sons-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: At first the princess had Taizong's favor, and so Yiai especially received gracious treatment; his ritual rank and salary differed utterly from the other imperial sons-in-law.

sentences.zh: 主既驕恣，謀黜遺直而奪其封爵，永徽中誣告遺直無禮於己。

translations.literal: The princess, being proud and willful, plotted to remove Yizhi and seize his enfeoffment; in the Yonghui era she falsely accused Yizhi of treating her without ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The princess, being proud and willful, plotted to remove Yizhi and seize his enfeoffment; in the Yonghui era she falsely accused Yizhi of treating her without ceremony.

sentences.zh: 高宗令長孫無忌鞫其事，因得公主與遺愛謀反之狀。

translations.literal: Gaozong ordered Zhangsun Wuji to examine the matter and thereby obtained evidence that the princess and Yiai had plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong ordered Zhangsun Wuji to examine the matter and thereby obtained evidence that the princess and Yiai had plotted rebellion.

sentences.zh: 遺愛伏誅，公主賜自盡，諸子配流嶺表。

translations.literal: Yiai was executed; the princess was ordered to take her own life; the sons were sent into exile beyond the Lingnan range.
translations.idiomatic: Yiai was executed; the princess was ordered to take her own life; the sons were sent into exile beyond the Lingnan range.

sentences.zh: 遺直以父功特宥之，除名爲庶人。

translations.literal: Yizhi was specially pardoned because of his father's merit, stripped of his name, and made a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: Yizhi was specially pardoned because of his father's merit, stripped of his name, and made a commoner.

sentences.zh: 停玄齡配享。

translations.literal: Xuanling's shared sacrifice was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanling's shared sacrifice was stopped.

sentences.zh: 杜如晦，字克明，京兆杜陵人也。

translations.literal: Du Ruhui, styled Keming, was a man of Duling in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Du Ruhui, styled Keming, was a man of Duling in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 曾祖皎，周贈開府儀同、大將軍、遂州刺史。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Jiao was posthumously enfeoffed in Zhou as General of the Gate with the same precedence as the Three Excellencies, Grand General, and Prefect of Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Jiao was posthumously enfeoffed in Zhou as General of the Gate with the same precedence as the Three Excellencies, Grand General, and Prefect of Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 高祖徽，周河內太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Hui was Prefect of Henei in Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Hui was Prefect of Henei in Zhou.

sentences.zh: 祖果，周溫州刺史，入隋，工部尚書、義興公，《周書》有傳。

translations.literal: His grandfather Guo was Prefect of Wen in Zhou; entering Sui, he was Minister of Works and Duke of Yixing; he has a biography in the Book of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Guo was Prefect of Wen in Zhou; entering Sui, he was Minister of Works and Duke of Yixing; he has a biography in the Book of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 父吒，隋昌州長史。

translations.literal: His father Tuo was Chief Administrator of Changzhou in Sui.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tuo was Chief Administrator of Changzhou in Sui.

sentences.zh: 如晦少聰悟，好談文史。

translations.literal: Ruhui was clever and perceptive from youth and loved to discuss literature and history.
translations.idiomatic: Ruhui was clever and perceptive from youth and loved to discuss literature and history.

sentences.zh: 隋大業中以常調預選，吏部侍郎高孝基深所器重，顧謂之曰：「公有應變之才，當爲棟樑之用，願保崇令德。

translations.literal: In the Daye era of Sui he entered selection by regular quota; Vice Minister of Personnel Gao Xiaoji deeply valued him, turned to him and said: "You have talent for meeting change and should serve as timber for the ridgepole; I wish you would preserve and exalt your fine virtue.
translations.idiomatic: In the Daye era of Sui he entered selection by regular quota; Vice Minister of Personnel Gao Xiaoji deeply valued him, turned to him and said: "You have talent for meeting change and should serve as timber for the ridgepole; I wish you would preserve and exalt your fine virtue.

sentences.zh: 今欲俯就卑職，爲須少祿俸耳。」

translations.literal: Now I wish to descend to a humble post, only for a little salary.""
translations.idiomatic: Now I wish to descend to a humble post, only for a little salary.""

sentences.zh: 遂補滏陽尉，尋棄官而歸。

translations.literal: He was then appointed sheriff of Fuyang; soon he abandoned the office and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed sheriff of Fuyang; soon he abandoned the office and returned home.

sentences.zh: 太宗平京城，引爲秦王府兵曹參軍，俄遷陝州總管府長史。

translations.literal: When Taizong pacified the capital, he was summoned as Military Administrative Aide of the Prince of Qin's household and soon promoted to Chief Administrator of the Shaanzhou Area Command.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong pacified the capital, he was summoned as Military Administrative Aide of the Prince of Qin's household and soon promoted to Chief Administrator of the Shaanzhou Area Command.

sentences.zh: 時府中多英俊，被外遷者眾，太宗患之。

translations.literal: At that time the household had many outstanding men, and many were transferred outward; Taizong was troubled by this.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the household had many outstanding men, and many were transferred outward; Taizong was troubled by this.

sentences.zh: 記室房玄齡曰：「府僚去者雖多，蓋不足惜。

translations.literal: Recorder Fang Xuanling said: "Though many staff members have left, that is scarcely to be regretted.
translations.idiomatic: Recorder Fang Xuanling said: "Though many staff members have left, that is scarcely to be regretted.

sentences.zh: 杜如晦聰明識達，王佐才也。
