translations.literal: Du Ruhui is intelligent, knowing, and penetrating—talent to assist a king.
translations.idiomatic: Du Ruhui is intelligent, knowing, and penetrating—talent to assist a king.

sentences.zh: 若大王守籓端拱，無所用之；

translations.literal: If the great king keeps the fief with folded hands and does nothing, he has no use for him;
translations.idiomatic: If the great king keeps the fief with folded hands and does nothing, he has no use for him;

sentences.zh: 必欲經營四方，非此人莫可。」

translations.literal: if you must manage the four quarters, none but this man will do."
translations.idiomatic: if you must manage the four quarters, none but this man will do."

sentences.zh: 太宗大驚曰：「爾不言，幾失此人矣！」

translations.literal: Taizong was greatly startled and said: "Had you not spoken, I would almost have lost this man!"
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was greatly startled and said: "Had you not spoken, I would almost have lost this man!"

sentences.zh: 遂奏爲府屬。

translations.literal: He then memorialized to make him a household staff member.
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized to make him a household staff member.

sentences.zh: 後從征薛仁杲、劉武周、王世充、竇建德，嘗參謀帷幄。

translations.literal: Afterward he followed the campaigns against Xue Rengao, Liu Wuzhou, Wang Shichong, and Dou Jiande, and often took part in planning within the tent.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he followed the campaigns against Xue Rengao, Liu Wuzhou, Wang Shichong, and Dou Jiande, and often took part in planning within the tent.

sentences.zh: 時軍國多事，剖斷如流，深爲時輩所服。

translations.literal: At that time military and state affairs were many; his decisions flowed like water, and the men of the age deeply submitted to him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time military and state affairs were many; his decisions flowed like water, and the men of the age deeply submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 累遷陝東道大行台司勳郎中，封建平縣男，食邑三百戸。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Director of Meritorious Service in the Shaanxi Eastern Circuit Grand Secretariat, enfeoffed as Baron of Pingping with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Director of Meritorious Service in the Shaanxi Eastern Circuit Grand Secretariat, enfeoffed as Baron of Pingping with a fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 尋以本官兼文學館學士。

translations.literal: Soon he held that office concurrently as a scholar of the Literary Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he held that office concurrently as a scholar of the Literary Hall.

sentences.zh: 天策府建，以爲從事中郎，畫像於丹青者十有八人，而如晦爲冠首，令文學褚亮爲之贊曰：「建平文雅，休有烈光。

translations.literal: When the Heavenly Stratagem Office was established, he was made Attendant Gentleman; of the eighteen men painted in colors, Ruhui stood first. Literary Scholar Chu Liang was ordered to compose a eulogy for him, saying: "Establishing peace with literary elegance, he has a blazing glory.
translations.idiomatic: When the Heavenly Stratagem Office was established, he was made Attendant Gentleman; of the eighteen men painted in colors, Ruhui stood first. Literary Scholar Chu Liang was ordered to compose a eulogy for him, saying: "Establishing peace with literary elegance, he has a blazing glory.

sentences.zh: 懷忠履義，身立名揚。」

translations.literal: Cherishing loyalty and treading righteousness, he stands and makes his name resound."
translations.idiomatic: Cherishing loyalty and treading righteousness, he stands and makes his name resound."

sentences.zh: 其見重如此。

translations.literal: He was valued to this degree.
translations.idiomatic: He was valued to this degree.

sentences.zh: 隱太子深忌之，謂齊王元吉曰：「秦王府中所可憚者，唯杜如晦與房玄齡耳。」

translations.literal: The Hidden Crown Prince deeply feared him and said to Prince of Qi Yuanji: "Among those to be feared in the Prince of Qin's household, only Du Ruhui and Fang Xuanling."
translations.idiomatic: The Hidden Crown Prince deeply feared him and said to Prince of Qi Yuanji: "Among those to be feared in the Prince of Qin's household, only Du Ruhui and Fang Xuanling."

sentences.zh: 因譖之於高祖，乃與玄齡同被斥逐。

translations.literal: He therefore slandered them to Gaozu, and Ruhui was expelled together with Xuanling.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore slandered them to Gaozu, and Ruhui was expelled together with Xuanling.

sentences.zh: 後又潛入畫策，及事捷，與房玄齡功等，擢拜太子左庶子，俄遷兵部尚書，進封蔡國公，賜實封千三百戸。

translations.literal: Afterward he secretly entered to draw up plans; when the affair succeeded, his merit equaled Fang Xuanling's. He was promoted Left Assistant of the Crown Prince, soon moved to Minister of War, advanced to Duke of Cai, and granted a substantial fief of one thousand three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he secretly entered to draw up plans; when the affair succeeded, his merit equaled Fang Xuanling's. He was promoted Left Assistant of the Crown Prince, soon moved to Minister of War, advanced to Duke of Cai, and granted a substantial fief of one thousand three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二年，以本官檢校侍中，攝吏部尚書，仍總監東宮兵馬事，號爲稱職。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenguan, holding his original office as acting Palace Attendant and provisional Minister of Personnel, he still oversaw the Eastern Palace's military and horse affairs and was called competent.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenguan, holding his original office as acting Palace Attendant and provisional Minister of Personnel, he still oversaw the Eastern Palace's military and horse affairs and was called competent.

sentences.zh: 三年，代長孫無忌爲尚書右僕射，仍知選事，與房玄齡共掌朝政。

translations.literal: In the third year he replaced Zhangsun Wuji as Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, still managing selection affairs, and with Fang Xuanling jointly held court governance.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he replaced Zhangsun Wuji as Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, still managing selection affairs, and with Fang Xuanling jointly held court governance.

sentences.zh: 至於台閣規模及典章人物，皆二人所定，甚獲當代之譽，談良相者，至今稱房、杜焉。

translations.literal: As for the platform and pavilion structure and the statutes and personnel, both men fixed them; they greatly won the praise of the age, and those who speak of good chancellors to this day still name Fang and Du.
translations.idiomatic: As for the platform and pavilion structure and the statutes and personnel, both men fixed them; they greatly won the praise of the age, and those who speak of good chancellors to this day still name Fang and Du.

sentences.zh: 如晦以高孝基有知人之鑑，爲其樹神道碑以紀其德。

translations.literal: Ruhui, because Gao Xiaoji had the mirror of knowing men, erected a spirit-way stele for him to record his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Ruhui, because Gao Xiaoji had the mirror of knowing men, erected a spirit-way stele for him to record his virtue.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，遇疾，表請解職，許之，祿賜特依舊。

translations.literal: That winter he fell ill, submitted a memorial asking to resign his office, was permitted, and salary and gifts followed the old standard.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he fell ill, submitted a memorial asking to resign his office, was permitted, and salary and gifts followed the old standard.

sentences.zh: 太宗深憂其疾，頻遣使存問，名醫上藥，相望於道。

translations.literal: Taizong deeply worried over his illness, repeatedly sent envoys to inquire after him, and famous physicians and superior medicines followed one another on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong deeply worried over his illness, repeatedly sent envoys to inquire after him, and famous physicians and superior medicines followed one another on the road.

sentences.zh: 四年，疾篤，令皇太子就第臨問，上親幸其宅，撫之流涕，賜物千段；

translations.literal: In the fourth year, when his illness was grave, the Crown Prince was ordered to visit his house and inquire; the emperor personally visited his residence, stroked him and wept, and granted a thousand bolts of goods;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, when his illness was grave, the Crown Prince was ordered to visit his house and inquire; the emperor personally visited his residence, stroked him and wept, and granted a thousand bolts of goods;

sentences.zh: 及其未終，見子拜官，遂超遷其子左千牛構爲尚舍奉御。

translations.literal: before he had finished, he saw his son receive appointment, and at once promoted his son Gou, Left Thousand-Bolt Guard, to Director of the Palace Commissary.
translations.idiomatic: before he had finished, he saw his son receive appointment, and at once promoted his son Gou, Left Thousand-Bolt Guard, to Director of the Palace Commissary.

sentences.zh: 尋薨，年四十六。

translations.literal: Soon he died, aged forty-six.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he died, aged forty-six.

sentences.zh: 太宗哭之甚慟，廢朝三日，贈司空，徙封萊國公，諡曰成。

translations.literal: Taizong wept for him with great grief, suspended court for three days, posthumously enfeoffed him as Minister of Works, transferred his enfeoffment to Duke of Lai, with the posthumous title Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong wept for him with great grief, suspended court for three days, posthumously enfeoffed him as Minister of Works, transferred his enfeoffment to Duke of Lai, with the posthumous title Cheng.

sentences.zh: 太宗手詔著作郎虞世南曰：「朕與如晦，君臣義重。

translations.literal: Taizong wrote in his own hand to Compiler Yu Shinan: "I and Ruhui had a weighty bond of ruler and minister.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong wrote in his own hand to Compiler Yu Shinan: "I and Ruhui had a weighty bond of ruler and minister.

sentences.zh: 不幸奄從物化，追念勳舊，痛悼於懷。

translations.literal: Unhappily he suddenly followed transformation; recalling his meritorious service of old, grief and mourning fill the breast.
translations.idiomatic: Unhappily he suddenly followed transformation; recalling his meritorious service of old, grief and mourning fill the breast.

sentences.zh: 卿體吾此意，爲制碑文也。」

translations.literal: Take my meaning and compose the stele inscription.""
translations.idiomatic: Take my meaning and compose the stele inscription.""

sentences.zh: 太宗後因食瓜而美，愴然悼之，遂輟食之半，遣使奠於靈座。

translations.literal: Later, when Taizong ate melon and found it fine, he mournfully grieved for Ruhui, stopped eating half of it, and sent an envoy to offer sacrifice at the spirit seat.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Taizong ate melon and found it fine, he mournfully grieved for Ruhui, stopped eating half of it, and sent an envoy to offer sacrifice at the spirit seat.

sentences.zh: 又嘗賜房玄齡黃銀帶，顧謂玄齡曰：「昔如晦與公同心輔朕，今日所賜，唯獨見公。」

translations.literal: He also once granted Fang Xuanling a yellow-silver belt, turned to Xuanling and said: "In former days Ruhui and you together assisted me with one heart; of what is granted today, you alone are seen.""
translations.idiomatic: He also once granted Fang Xuanling a yellow-silver belt, turned to Xuanling and said: "In former days Ruhui and you together assisted me with one heart; of what is granted today, you alone are seen.""

sentences.zh: 因泫然流涕。

translations.literal: He thereupon wept with streaming tears.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon wept with streaming tears.

sentences.zh: 又曰：「朕聞黃銀多爲鬼神所畏。」

translations.literal: He also said: "I have heard that yellow silver is much feared by ghosts and spirits.""
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "I have heard that yellow silver is much feared by ghosts and spirits.""

sentences.zh: 命取黃金帶遣玄齡親送於靈所。

translations.literal: He ordered a gold belt taken and sent Xuanling in person to deliver it to the spirit place.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered a gold belt taken and sent Xuanling in person to deliver it to the spirit place.

sentences.zh: 其後太宗忽夢見如晦若平生，及曉，以告玄齡，言之歔欷，令送御饌以祭焉。

translations.literal: Afterward Taizong suddenly dreamed of Ruhui as in life; at dawn he told Xuanling, spoke with sighs and sobs, and ordered imperial fare sent as sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Taizong suddenly dreamed of Ruhui as in life; at dawn he told Xuanling, spoke with sighs and sobs, and ordered imperial fare sent as sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 明年如晦亡日，太宗復遣尚宮至第慰問其妻子，其國官府佐並不之罷。

translations.literal: The next year on the anniversary of Ruhui's death, Taizong again sent a palace official to his house to console his wife and children; the officials of his state household were not dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The next year on the anniversary of Ruhui's death, Taizong again sent a palace official to his house to console his wife and children; the officials of his state household were not dismissed.

sentences.zh: 終始恩遇，未之有焉。

translations.literal: Favor from first to last—there has never been the like.
translations.idiomatic: Favor from first to last—there has never been the like.

sentences.zh: 子構襲爵，官至慈州刺史，坐弟荷謀逆，徙於嶺表而卒。

translations.literal: His son Gou inherited the title, reached Prefect of Ci, and because his younger brother He plotted rebellion was sent into exile beyond the Lingnan range, where he died.
translations.idiomatic: His son Gou inherited the title, reached Prefect of Ci, and because his younger brother He plotted rebellion was sent into exile beyond the Lingnan range, where he died.

sentences.zh: 初，荷以功臣子尚城陽公主，賜爵襄陽郡公，授尚乘奉御。

translations.literal: At first He, as the son of a meritorious minister, married Princess Chengyang, was enfeoffed Duke of Xiangyang, and appointed Director of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: At first He, as the son of a meritorious minister, married Princess Chengyang, was enfeoffed Duke of Xiangyang, and appointed Director of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，與太子承乾謀反，坐斬。

translations.literal: In the Zhenguan era he plotted rebellion with Crown Prince Chengqian and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenguan era he plotted rebellion with Crown Prince Chengqian and was executed.

sentences.zh: 如晦弟楚客，少隨叔父淹沒於王世充。

translations.literal: Ruhui's younger brother Chuke in youth followed his uncle Yan and was submerged in Wang Shichong's domain.
translations.idiomatic: Ruhui's younger brother Chuke in youth followed his uncle Yan and was submerged in Wang Shichong's domain.

sentences.zh: 淹素與如晦兄弟不睦，譖如晦兄於王行滿，王世充殺之，並囚楚客，幾至餓死，楚客竟無怨色。

translations.literal: Yan had long been at odds with Ruhui and his brothers; he slandered Ruhui's elder brother to Wang Xingman, and Wang Shichong killed him and also imprisoned Chuke, who nearly starved to death—yet Chuke showed no resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had long been at odds with Ruhui and his brothers; he slandered Ruhui's elder brother to Wang Xingman, and Wang Shichong killed him and also imprisoned Chuke, who nearly starved to death—yet Chuke showed no resentment.

sentences.zh: 洛陽平，淹當死，楚客泣涕請如晦救之。

translations.literal: When Luoyang was pacified, Yan was due for death; Chuke wept and begged Ruhui to save him.
translations.idiomatic: When Luoyang was pacified, Yan was due for death; Chuke wept and begged Ruhui to save him.

sentences.zh: 如晦初不從，楚客曰：「叔已殺大兄，今兄又結恨棄叔，一門之內，相殺而盡，豈不痛哉！」

translations.literal: At first Ruhui would not agree; Chuke said: "The uncle already killed the elder brother; now the elder brother again bears hatred and abandons the uncle—within one gate, killing one another to the end—is that not pain!""
translations.idiomatic: At first Ruhui would not agree; Chuke said: "The uncle already killed the elder brother; now the elder brother again bears hatred and abandons the uncle—within one gate, killing one another to the end—is that not pain!""

sentences.zh: 因欲自刎。

translations.literal: He thereupon wished to cut his own throat.
translations.idiomatic: He thereupon wished to cut his own throat.

sentences.zh: 如晦感其言，請於太宗，淹遂蒙恩宥。

translations.literal: Ruhui was moved by his words and asked Taizong; Yan then received gracious pardon.
translations.idiomatic: Ruhui was moved by his words and asked Taizong; Yan then received gracious pardon.

sentences.zh: 楚客因隱於嵩山。

translations.literal: Chuke therefore hid on Mount Song.
translations.idiomatic: Chuke therefore hid on Mount Song.

sentences.zh: 貞觀四年，召拜給事中，上謂曰：「聞卿山居日久，志意甚高，自非宰相之任，則不能出，何有是理耶？

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhenguan he was summoned and appointed Supervising Secretary; the emperor said to him: "I hear you have dwelt long in the mountains, and your will is very high; unless the post is chancellor, you cannot come out—is there such a principle?
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhenguan he was summoned and appointed Supervising Secretary; the emperor said to him: "I hear you have dwelt long in the mountains, and your will is very high; unless the post is chancellor, you cannot come out—is there such a principle?

sentences.zh: 夫涉遠者必自邇，升高者必自下，但在官爲眾所許，無慮官之不大。

translations.literal: To travel far one must begin from what is near; to climb high one must begin from what is low—but if in office one is approved by the masses, one need not worry that the office will not be great.
translations.idiomatic: To travel far one must begin from what is near; to climb high one must begin from what is low—but if in office one is approved by the masses, one need not worry that the office will not be great.

sentences.zh: 爾兄雖與我體異，其心猶一，於我國家非無大功。

translations.literal: Though your elder brother differs from me in body, his heart is still one; for our state he has no small great merit.
translations.idiomatic: Though your elder brother differs from me in body, his heart is still one; for our state he has no small great merit.

sentences.zh: 爲憶爾兄，意欲見爾。

translations.literal: Recalling your elder brother, I wish to see you.
translations.idiomatic: Recalling your elder brother, I wish to see you.

sentences.zh: 宜識朕意，繼爾兄之忠義也。」

translations.literal: You should know my intent and continue your elder brother's loyal righteousness."
translations.idiomatic: You should know my intent and continue your elder brother's loyal righteousness."

sentences.zh: 拜楚客蒲州刺史，甚有能名。

translations.literal: Chuke was appointed Prefect of Pu and had a great name for ability.
translations.idiomatic: Chuke was appointed Prefect of Pu and had a great name for ability.

sentences.zh: 後歷魏王府長史，拜工部尚書，攝魏王泰府事。

translations.literal: Later he served as Chief Administrator of Prince of Wei's household, was appointed Minister of Works, and held affairs of Prince of Wei Tai's household in commission.
translations.idiomatic: Later he served as Chief Administrator of Prince of Wei's household, was appointed Minister of Works, and held affairs of Prince of Wei Tai's household in commission.

sentences.zh: 楚客知太宗不悅承乾，魏王泰又潛令楚客友朝臣用事者，至有懷金以賂之，因説泰聰明，可爲嫡嗣。

translations.literal: Chuke knew Taizong was displeased with Chengqian and that Prince of Wei Tai also secretly had Chuke befriend court officials in power; some even brought gold to bribe them, and he urged that Tai was intelligent and could be made heir.
translations.idiomatic: Chuke knew Taizong was displeased with Chengqian and that Prince of Wei Tai also secretly had Chuke befriend court officials in power; some even brought gold to bribe them, and he urged that Tai was intelligent and could be made heir.

sentences.zh: 人或以聞，太宗隱而不言。

translations.literal: Some reported this; Taizong concealed it and did not speak.
translations.idiomatic: Some reported this; Taizong concealed it and did not speak.

sentences.zh: 及釁發，太宗始揚其事，以其兄有佐命功，免死，廢於家。

translations.literal: When the breach broke open, Taizong at last publicized the matter; because his elder brother had merit in founding the mandate, he was spared death and degraded at home.
translations.idiomatic: When the breach broke open, Taizong at last publicized the matter; because his elder brother had merit in founding the mandate, he was spared death and degraded at home.

sentences.zh: 尋授處化令，卒。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed magistrate of Chuhua and died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was appointed magistrate of Chuhua and died.

sentences.zh: 如晦叔父淹。

translations.literal: Ruhui's uncle Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Ruhui's uncle Yan.

sentences.zh: 淹，字執禮。

translations.literal: Yan, styled Zhili.
translations.idiomatic: Yan, styled Zhili.

sentences.zh: 祖業，周豫州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Ye was Prefect of Yu in Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Ye was Prefect of Yu in Zhou.

sentences.zh: 父征，河內太守。

translations.literal: His father Zheng was Prefect of Henei.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zheng was Prefect of Henei.

sentences.zh: 淹聰辯多才藝，弱冠有美名，與同郡韋福嗣爲莫逆之交，相與謀曰：「上好用嘉遁，蘇威以幽人見徵，擢居美職。」

translations.literal: Yan was clever in debate and had many arts and skills; in his weak-capped years he had a fine name. With Wei Fuqi of the same commandery he was friends beyond measure; together they plotted and said: "The ruler above loves worthy recluses; Su Wei, as a man in seclusion, was summoned and promoted to a fine post.""
translations.idiomatic: Yan was clever in debate and had many arts and skills; in his weak-capped years he had a fine name. With Wei Fuqi of the same commandery he was friends beyond measure; together they plotted and said: "The ruler above loves worthy recluses; Su Wei, as a man in seclusion, was summoned and promoted to a fine post.""

sentences.zh: 遂共入太白山，揚言隱逸，實欲邀求時譽。

translations.literal: They then together entered Mount Taibai, publicly declaring reclusion while in fact seeking reputation of the age.
translations.idiomatic: They then together entered Mount Taibai, publicly declaring reclusion while in fact seeking reputation of the age.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝聞而惡之，謫戍江表，後還鄕里。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui heard of it and hated them; they were banished to garrison on the Jiang south and later returned to their native place.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui heard of it and hated them; they were banished to garrison on the Jiang south and later returned to their native place.

sentences.zh: 雍州司馬高孝基上表薦之，授承奉郎。

translations.literal: Chief Administrator of Yongzhou Gao Xiaoji submitted a memorial recommending them; they were appointed Gentlemen for Attending Service.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Administrator of Yongzhou Gao Xiaoji submitted a memorial recommending them; they were appointed Gentlemen for Attending Service.

sentences.zh: 大業末，官至御史中丞。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daye era he reached Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daye era he reached Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 王世充僭號，署爲吏部，大見親用。

translations.literal: When Wang Shichong usurped the title, he was appointed to the Ministry of Personnel and was greatly trusted and used.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Shichong usurped the title, he was appointed to the Ministry of Personnel and was greatly trusted and used.

sentences.zh: 及洛陽平，初不得調，淹將委質於隱太子。

translations.literal: When Luoyang was pacified, at first he received no appointment; Yan was about to pledge allegiance to the Hidden Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: When Luoyang was pacified, at first he received no appointment; Yan was about to pledge allegiance to the Hidden Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 時封德彝典選，以告房玄齡，恐隱太子得之，長其奸計，於是遽啟太宗，引爲天策府兵曹參軍、文學館學士。

translations.literal: At that time Feng Deyi managed selection; he told Fang Xuanling, fearing the Hidden Crown Prince would obtain him and lengthen his wicked plans; he therefore hastily reported to Taizong, who summoned Yan as Military Administrative Aide of the Heavenly Stratagem Office and Literary Hall scholar.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Feng Deyi managed selection; he told Fang Xuanling, fearing the Hidden Crown Prince would obtain him and lengthen his wicked plans; he therefore hastily reported to Taizong, who summoned Yan as Military Administrative Aide of the Heavenly Stratagem Office and Literary Hall scholar.

sentences.zh: 武德八年，慶州總管楊文幹作亂，辭連東宮，歸罪於淹及王珪、韋挺等，並流於越巂。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Wude, Area Commander Yang Wengan of Qingzhou rebelled; his words implicated the Eastern Palace, and blame was laid on Yan together with Wang Gui, Wei Ting, and others; all were sent into exile in Yuexi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Wude, Area Commander Yang Wengan of Qingzhou rebelled; his words implicated the Eastern Palace, and blame was laid on Yan together with Wang Gui, Wei Ting, and others; all were sent into exile in Yuexi.

sentences.zh: 太宗知淹非罪，贈以黃金三百兩。

translations.literal: Taizong knew Yan was not guilty and sent him three hundred bolts of yellow gold.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong knew Yan was not guilty and sent him three hundred bolts of yellow gold.

sentences.zh: 及即位，徵拜御史大夫，封安吉郡公，賜實封四百戸。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, Yan was summoned as Censor-in-Chief, enfeoffed Duke of Anji, and granted a substantial fief of four hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong took the throne, Yan was summoned as Censor-in-Chief, enfeoffed Duke of Anji, and granted a substantial fief of four hundred households.

sentences.zh: 以淹多識典故，特詔東宮儀式簿領，並取淹節度。

translations.literal: Because Yan knew many precedents and statutes, a special edict took the Eastern Palace's ritual forms and ledgers and had Yan direct them all.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yan knew many precedents and statutes, a special edict took the Eastern Palace's ritual forms and ledgers and had Yan direct them all.

sentences.zh: 尋判吏部尚書，參議朝政。

translations.literal: Soon he was assigned Minister of Personnel and took part in deliberating court governance.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was assigned Minister of Personnel and took part in deliberating court governance.

sentences.zh: 前後表薦四十餘人，後多知名者。

translations.literal: Before and after he submitted memorials recommending more than forty men; many later became well known.
translations.idiomatic: Before and after he submitted memorials recommending more than forty men; many later became well known.

sentences.zh: 淹嘗薦刑部員外郎郅懷道，太宗因問淹：「懷道才行何如？」

translations.literal: Yan once recommended Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice Chi Huaidao; Taizong therefore asked Yan: "How are Huaidao's conduct and talent?""
translations.idiomatic: Yan once recommended Vice Director of the Ministry of Justice Chi Huaidao; Taizong therefore asked Yan: "How are Huaidao's conduct and talent?""

sentences.zh: 淹對曰：「懷道在隋日作吏部主事，甚有清慎之名。

translations.literal: Yan replied: "In Sui days Huaidao served as chief clerk in the Ministry of Personnel and had a great name for purity and caution.
translations.idiomatic: Yan replied: "In Sui days Huaidao served as chief clerk in the Ministry of Personnel and had a great name for purity and caution.

sentences.zh: 又煬帝向江都之日，召百官問去住之計。

translations.literal: Also, on the day Emperor Yang went toward Jiangdu, he summoned the hundred officials to ask their plans for going or staying.
translations.idiomatic: Also, on the day Emperor Yang went toward Jiangdu, he summoned the hundred officials to ask their plans for going or staying.

sentences.zh: 時行計已決，公卿皆阿旨請去，懷道官位極卑，獨言不可。

translations.literal: At that time the plan to go was already decided; the high ministers all flattered the intent and asked to go; Huaidao's rank was extremely low, yet he alone said it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the plan to go was already decided; the high ministers all flattered the intent and asked to go; Huaidao's rank was extremely low, yet he alone said it could not be done.

sentences.zh: 臣目見此事。」

translations.literal: Your servant saw this matter with his own eyes.""
translations.idiomatic: Your servant saw this matter with his own eyes.""

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「卿爾可從何計？」

translations.literal: Taizong said: "You then—what plan did you follow?""
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said: "You then—what plan did you follow?""

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣從行計。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Your servant followed the plan to go.""
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Your servant followed the plan to go.""

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「事君之義，有犯無隱。

translations.literal: Taizong said: "In serving a ruler, the principle is to remonstrate though it offend and hide nothing.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said: "In serving a ruler, the principle is to remonstrate though it offend and hide nothing.

sentences.zh: 卿稱懷道爲是，何因自不正諫？」

translations.literal: You call Huaidao right—why did you yourself not remonstrate directly?"
translations.idiomatic: You call Huaidao right—why did you yourself not remonstrate directly?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣爾日不居重任，又知諫必不從，徒死無益。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Your servant then did not hold a weighty post, and also knew that remonstrance would certainly not be followed—dying in vain would have no benefit.""
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Your servant then did not hold a weighty post, and also knew that remonstrance would certainly not be followed—dying in vain would have no benefit.""

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「孔子稱從父之命，未爲孝子。

translations.literal: Taizong said: "Confucius said, 'Obeying a father's command is not yet being a filial son.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said: "Confucius said, 'Obeying a father's command is not yet being a filial son.

sentences.zh: 故父有爭子，國有爭臣。

translations.literal: Therefore a father has a son who contends, and a state has a minister who contends.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore a father has a son who contends, and a state has a minister who contends.

sentences.zh: 若以主之無道，何爲仍仕其世？

translations.literal: If the ruler above is without the Way, why still serve his age?
translations.idiomatic: If the ruler above is without the Way, why still serve his age?

sentences.zh: 既食其祿，豈得不匡其非？」

translations.literal: Since one eats his salary, how can one not set right his wrongs?"
translations.idiomatic: Since one eats his salary, how can one not set right his wrongs?"

sentences.zh: 因謂群臣曰：「公等各言諫事如何？」

translations.literal: He therefore said to the assembled ministers: "Each of you—speak of remonstrance, how is it?"
translations.idiomatic: He therefore said to the assembled ministers: "Each of you—speak of remonstrance, how is it?"

sentences.zh: 王珪曰：「昔比干諫紂而死，孔子稱其仁；

translations.literal: Wang Gui said: "In former days Bi Gan remonstrated with Zhou and died; Confucius called him humane;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui said: "In former days Bi Gan remonstrated with Zhou and died; Confucius called him humane;

sentences.zh: 洩冶諫而被戮，孔子曰：『民之多辟，無自立辟。』

translations.literal: Xie Ye remonstrated and was slaughtered; Confucius said: 'When the people have many evils, do not establish evils of your own.
translations.idiomatic: Xie Ye remonstrated and was slaughtered; Confucius said: 'When the people have many evils, do not establish evils of your own.

sentences.zh: 是則祿重責深，理須極諫；

translations.literal: Thus when salary is heavy and responsibility deep, reason requires utmost remonstrance;
translations.idiomatic: Thus when salary is heavy and responsibility deep, reason requires utmost remonstrance;

sentences.zh: 官卑望下，許其從容。」

translations.literal: when office is low and expectation small, one may be allowed leeway.""
translations.idiomatic: when office is low and expectation small, one may be allowed leeway.""

sentences.zh: 太宗又召淹，笑謂曰：「卿在隋日，可以位下不言；

translations.literal: Taizong again summoned Yan, smiled and said to him: "You in Sui days, with rank low, might not speak;
translations.idiomatic: Taizong again summoned Yan, smiled and said to him: "You in Sui days, with rank low, might not speak;

sentences.zh: 近仕世充，何不極諫？」

translations.literal: recently serving Shichong, why not remonstrate to the utmost?""
translations.idiomatic: recently serving Shichong, why not remonstrate to the utmost?""

sentences.zh: 對曰：「亦有諫，但不見從。」

translations.literal: He replied: "There was also remonstrance, but it was not followed.""
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "There was also remonstrance, but it was not followed.""

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「世充若修德從善，當不滅亡；

translations.literal: Taizong said: "If Shichong had cultivated virtue and followed goodness, he ought not to have perished;
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said: "If Shichong had cultivated virtue and followed goodness, he ought not to have perished;

sentences.zh: 既無道拒諫，卿何免禍？」

translations.literal: since he was without the Way and rejected remonstrance, how did you escape calamity?""
translations.idiomatic: since he was without the Way and rejected remonstrance, how did you escape calamity?""

sentences.zh: 淹無以對。

translations.literal: Yan had nothing to reply.
translations.idiomatic: Yan had nothing to reply.

sentences.zh: 太宗又曰：「卿在今日，可爲備任，復欲極諫否？」

translations.literal: Taizong also said: "You in the present day can fill a full post—do you again wish to remonstrate to the utmost?""
translations.idiomatic: Taizong also said: "You in the present day can fill a full post—do you again wish to remonstrate to the utmost?""

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣在今日，必盡死無隱。

translations.literal: He replied: "Your servant in the present day will certainly exhaust death and hide nothing.
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "Your servant in the present day will certainly exhaust death and hide nothing.

sentences.zh: 且百里奚在虞虞亡，在秦秦霸，臣竊比之。」

translations.literal: Moreover, Baili Xi in Yu—Yu perished; in Qin—Qin became hegemon; your servant privately compares myself to him.""
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Baili Xi in Yu—Yu perished; in Qin—Qin became hegemon; your servant privately compares myself to him.""

sentences.zh: 太宗笑。

translations.literal: Taizong laughed.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong laughed.

sentences.zh: 時淹兼二職，而無清潔之譽，又素與無忌不協，爲時論所譏。

translations.literal: At that time Yan held two posts concurrently yet had no reputation for purity; he also had long been at odds with Wuji, and the talk of the age mocked him.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yan held two posts concurrently yet had no reputation for purity; he also had long been at odds with Wuji, and the talk of the age mocked him.

sentences.zh: 及有疾，太宗親自臨問，賜帛三百匹。

translations.literal: When he fell ill, Taizong personally visited and inquired, granting three hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill, Taizong personally visited and inquired, granting three hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 貞觀二年卒，贈尚書右僕射，諡曰襄。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenguan he died, posthumously enfeoffed Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, with the posthumous title Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhenguan he died, posthumously enfeoffed Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, with the posthumous title Xiang.

sentences.zh: 子敬同襲爵，官至鴻臚少卿。

translations.literal: His son Jingtong inherited the title and reached Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jingtong inherited the title and reached Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 敬同子從則，中宗時爲蒲州刺史。

translations.literal: Jingtong's son Congze, in the Zhongzong era, was Prefect of Pu.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtong's son Congze, in the Zhongzong era, was Prefect of Pu.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：房、杜二公，皆以命世之才，遭逢明主，謀猷允協，以致昇平。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Fang and Du, the two lords, both possessed talent of an age, met enlightened rulers, and with plans and counsel in accord brought about ascending peace.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer says: Fang and Du, the two lords, both possessed talent of an age, met enlightened rulers, and with plans and counsel in accord brought about ascending peace.

sentences.zh: 議者以比漢之蕭、曹，信矣！

translations.literal: Those who discuss the matter compare them to Xiao and Cao of Han—truly so!
translations.idiomatic: Those who discuss the matter compare them to Xiao and Cao of Han—truly so!

sentences.zh: 然萊成之見用，文昭之所舉也。

translations.literal: Yet when Lai Cheng was employed, it was Wenzhao who recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet when Lai Cheng was employed, it was Wenzhao who recommended him.

sentences.zh: 世傳太宗嘗與文昭圖事，則曰「非如晦莫能籌之」。

translations.literal: The age transmits that Taizong once planned affairs with Wenzhao, who then said, "No one but Ruhui can plan this."
translations.idiomatic: The age transmits that Taizong once planned affairs with Wenzhao, who then said, "No one but Ruhui can plan this."

sentences.zh: 及如晦至焉，竟從玄齡之策也。

translations.literal: When Ruhui arrived, in the end they followed Xuanling's plan.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruhui arrived, in the end they followed Xuanling's plan.

sentences.zh: 蓋房知杜之能斷大事，杜知房之善建嘉謀，裨諶草創，東里潤色，相須而成，俾無悔事，賢達用心，良有以也。

translations.literal: Fang knew Du's ability to decide great affairs; Du knew Fang's skill in building fine plans—one assisted in the first drafting, the other polished in the eastern quarter; they needed one another to succeed, so that there were no regrettable affairs. That worthy men applied their hearts thus indeed has its reason.
translations.idiomatic: Fang knew Du's ability to decide great affairs; Du knew Fang's skill in building fine plans—one assisted in the first drafting, the other polished in the eastern quarter; they needed one another to succeed, so that there were no regrettable affairs. That worthy men applied their hearts thus indeed has its reason.

sentences.zh: 若以往哲方之，房則管仲、子產，杜則鮑叔、罕虎矣。

translations.literal: If compared with sages of old, Fang is Guan Zhong and Zichan; Du is Bao Shuya and Han Hu.
translations.idiomatic: If compared with sages of old, Fang is Guan Zhong and Zichan; Du is Bao Shuya and Han Hu.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：肇啟聖君，必生賢輔。

translations.literal: The eulogy says: When a sage ruler first opens the way, worthy assistants must be born.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogy says: When a sage ruler first opens the way, worthy assistants must be born.

sentences.zh: 猗歟二公，實開運祚。

translations.literal: How splendid, the two lords—they truly opened the fortune of the throne.
translations.idiomatic: How splendid, the two lords—they truly opened the fortune of the throne.

sentences.zh: 文含經緯，謀深夾輔。

translations.literal: In writing they held warp and woof; in counsel they aided deeply at the side.
translations.idiomatic: In writing they held warp and woof; in counsel they aided deeply at the side.

sentences.zh: 笙磬同音，唯房與杜。

translations.literal: Pipes and chimes in one tone—only Fang and Du.
translations.idiomatic: Pipes and chimes in one tone—only Fang and Du.
